There was a time in my life when I volunteered on the ambulance with two local EMS stations in Pennsylvania where I lived. I was a trained EMT and equipped to help a hurting person.

During my times of duty, I was prepared to run at a moment’s notice. I had no idea when my ever-present pager would sound an alarm. At night, I would sleep fully dressed in my EMT garb. My boots were parked by the door. My car was backed up to the house and the keys were lying on the nightstand. I was prepared!

Some nights my pager never sounded. Other nights, the pager would beep loudly, disturbing a deep sleep. All my preparation time paid off and within seconds of the alarm I was driving down the road. Every second counted. I had to be prepared at all times.

It is no secret that athletes who play in the Olympic games often dedicate most of their life toward preparing for the game. They want nothing more than to reach the goal of winning that medal. But they must prepare! They do not wake up one morning and decide to travel to the Olympics that day to compete for the gold medal. If they want to win, they need to prepare. If they want that gold medal award, they need to train.

By about the age of 14, a British athlete will have decided on which sport to focus. At that point, he will begin to pour his life into training. An incredible amount of commitment, resources, and investment is needed to compete on the highest stage. The average elite athlete trains six hours a day, six days a week, twelve months a year. His goal? To win!

One athlete said, “All the hard work will be worth it, though, to simply compete in front of a home crowd—and to win a medal would just be a dream come true.”

As a Kingdom Christian, I look at a quote like this and say, “how frivolous and empty.” But I ask you, young person: if they give everything that they have to win something so temporal, what are you giving to win something so eternal? What are you giving for a reward that will outlast anything on this earth—a reward that has value out of this world?

Paul used a runner as an example of how we should run in our Christian life: Know ye not that they which run in a race run all, but one receiveth the prize? So run, that ye may obtain –1Co 9:24. You are to run this race of the Christian life in such a way that you may win! I ask you, are you preparing to win? Are you running in such a way that you will win?

Let’s take a brief look at two observations from an Olympic athlete and then make practical applications to our spiritual walk.

Observation #1: Exercise must be an everyday occurrence for an athlete.

Pro athletes don’t train because they must. They grow up wanting nothing more than to play their sport for the rest of their lives. But to do so, they know that making exercise a part of everyday life is essential to winning. It doesn’t matter if they run, lift weights, or go for a walk, athletes in training will get into a habit of daily exercise. It is as much a part of their day as brushing their teeth or combing their hair.

And every man that striveth for the mastery is temperate in all things. Now they do it to obtain a corruptible crown; but we an incorruptible –1Co 9:25. As a Christian, if your goal is to be faithful to the end and win the race of your Christian life, then you will need to become serious about your spiritual exercises. In fact, daily spiritual exercises are essential to staying fit for this intense race.

Exercise must be an everyday occurrence for a Christian. Read your Bible as though your life depends on it—because it does! Pray and stay connected to Jesus with the same purpose of heart that an athlete drinks fluid. (Did you know that drinking fluids is the most important part of an athlete’s diet?) Pray as though your life depends on it—because it does!

Observation #2: An athlete in training gets the results he deserves.

It is so hard to get up early in the morning when you’re snuggled under the covers and it’s dark and cold outside. But an athlete in training knows that if he doesn’t get up to practice and exercise, he will lose. He knows that the more he exercises, the better chance he has of winning. An athlete in training knows that he will be rewarded for his time spent in preparing. There will be results from choosing to exercise.

That the righteousness of the law might be fulfilled in us, who walk not after the flesh, but after the Spirit. For they that are after the flesh do mind the things of the flesh; but they that are after the Spirit the things of the Spirit. For to be carnally minded is death; but to be spiritually minded is life and peace –Rom 8: 4-6.

As a Christian, what you feed will grow. You will either be feeding the flesh, or you will be feeding the Spirit. If you want to win the race and reach the reward of being restored to how you were really meant to live, then you will need to be spiritually minded and feed the things of the Spirit. Now let’s consider a partial list of things that depending how or why we do it, will determine whether we are feeding our flesh or the Spirit.

Hunting and getting meat for the freezer is a very natural activity for survival and has been done for centuries. But when you go hunting to get the biggest buck to boost your ego and self-esteem, that is feeding your flesh.

Listening to the world’s music will not do a thing to feed and exercise the spiritual man. But your flesh will be richly fed.

Following and/or playing in the professional sports world will not help you in winning the spiritual race. In fact, you will lose if you feed your flesh unheedingly.

Gluttony and/or consuming unhealthy food and drink will not help your spiritual man grow in the Lord. In fact, it will only feed your craving for more and more. Let’s be careful that whether we eat or drink we are doing it to God’s glory.

My dear friend, the simple fact remains: if you do not persevere in disciplining your spiritual life, you will lose! So, what are you exercising and feeding—your flesh or the Spirit? Remember, when the natural man grows, there is no more room for the spiritual man to grow.

Reaching Forth and Pressing Toward

Paul says, Brethren, I count not myself to have apprehended: but this one thing I do, forgetting those things which are behind, and reaching forth unto those things which are before, I press toward the mark for the prize of the high calling of God in Christ Jesus –Php 3:13-14.

There’s a pressing and a reaching that must happen in your Christian life if you want to win. You don’t just get by with doing the minimum in the Christian life—God calls that lukewarmness and the Bible says He will vomit a lukewarm person out of His mouth (see Rev. 3:16). God is not looking for half-hearted overcomers. He is looking for ‘more than conquerors’. There is no room for lukewarmness in the kingdom of God!

To prepare ourselves to win this race, we cannot get by without discipline and self-sacrifice. Are you a disciplined person in your spiritual life? How does it compare to your physical work and hobbies? Do you get up early for a physical sport you enjoy? Do you make sure you’re at your job on time?

Do you have the same drive to get up early and discipline yourself in your spiritual life? Do you reach for your Bible as eagerly as you reach for your softball glove? Do you reach for your Bible as eagerly as you reach for that can of pop? Do you reach for your Bible as eagerly as you reach for your gun or bow to go hunting? Do you reach for your Bible as eagerly as you reach for your phone? Do you spend more time focusing on your spiritual life than you do dressing yourself and combing your hair? Do you care more what your friends think or what Jesus thinks?

There’s a big social media craze to show everyone what you’re doing and gain approval of men. Viewing social media postings will rob you of your spiritual focus. Posting on social media sites for all to see feeds a craving for approval of men.

There are many social media sites and apps out there. However, there’s one app that creates similar cravings, but in a more subtle way. It’s an app that lets you tell others “what’s up”. This app is named WhatsApp. This app is very useful for texting, especially with our acquaintances who are overseas. But included in WhatsApp is a button called Status. It allows you to post things for others to see. It allows you to see what your friends are doing right now—what their status is!

Posting one’s activities and life’s events online for the world to see has become a gripping drive and craving for attention—a crave for the approval of men. If you feed this drive, it will grow. Ask yourself these questions, “Does posting my status on WhatsApp bring glory to God? Does checking social media sites to see what others are doing and how they are dressed draw me closer to God? Am I more eager to check the status of my friends than I am to open my Bible and check the status of my walk with God?” Is the time you spend on your phone making you better prepared to win this race?

The Demand for Your Time

How much time do you spend exercising? If an athlete would do one push-up a day, do you think he would win? If an athlete who desperately wants to win that gold medal would only walk 1/10 of a mile each day, do you think he would win?

So, as you prepare to meet God and win this race, is one Bible verse a day enough for you to win? Is one minute of prayer time each day with your Savior enough for you to fight the intense spiritual battles with the enemy?

Take time to read your Bible—your life depends on it for survival! Take time to pray—you cannot run this race without it!

“I got up early one morning, and rushed
right into the day;
I had so much to accomplish that I didn’t
have time to pray.
Problems just tumbled about me, and
heavier came each task;
“Why doesn’t God help me?” I wondered.
He answered, “You didn’t ask.”
I wanted to see joy and beauty, but the day
toiled on gray and bleak;
I wondered why God didn’t show me. He
said, “But you didn’t seek.”
I tried to come into God’s presence; I used
all my keys in the lock.
God gently and lovingly chided, “My
child, you didn’t knock.”
I woke up early this morning, and paused
before entering the day;
I had so much to accomplish that I had to
take time to pray.”
-anonymous

The demands for our time could not be greater. Technological conveniences are shaping our lives. Our booming economy is reaching for our time. We are living in spiritually dangerous times! Have the demands and distractions of life lessened your time in spiritual exercise? Does it concern you when your prayer time and Bible reading time diminishes because you simply don’t have time?

Remove Distractions

Wherefore seeing we also are compassed about with so great a cloud of witnesses, let us lay aside every weight, and the sin which doth so easily beset us, and let us run with patience the race that is set before us, –Heb 12:1.

The Greek word for weight describes it as a hindrance. Are there activities or habits that hinder you from giving all you have to run this race? Is there something that is hindering your exercise—your spiritual growth?

The Greek word for beset describes it as to distract or compete. Are there sins distracting you from the race? Are there things that you do that compete with your spiritual exercises?

Maybe busyness is the weight that’s hindering your race. Maybe spiritual apathy is your sin—apathy is a lack of interest or concern. You’ve gone to sleep spiritually, and you simply do not care. Maybe things the world highly esteems are competing with your spiritual life and exercise—things such as wealth, sports, and popularity. The world highly esteems clothing? Did you ever go shopping and buy a piece of clothing you didn’t really need, just because it was nice—a new style?

Maybe your weight or distraction is simply a lack of vision for the kingdom of God. The Bible says that where there is no vision, the people perish. If you do not have a vision, you will perish. Plainly stated, you will lose the race and go to hell if you do not have a vision for the Kingdom of God!

I encourage you to open your life before the Lord—ask Him these serious questions.

  • “God, are my priorities straight?”
  • “God, do I value what you value?”
  • “God, am I lacking vision?”
  • “God, am I reaching for things that don’t last?”
  • “God, am I too busy running after things that hinder my running?”
  • “God, what is my weight—what is my hindrance?”

This is all about preparing to meet the Lord and preparing for our eternal destiny. It’s all about being effective soldiers in His kingdom. If you refuse to run the race well here on earth and be faithful, do you think God wants you in heaven?

Maybe you need to get desperate with God. Maybe you need to make some radical changes in your life—changes to your schedule, your focus, your activities, your pursuits.

No Man Knows the Time

All of us have an appointed time of death on God’s calendar. You have no idea which day of which year your name is listed on God’s calendar. It could be that you have only one more week here on this earth.

There is also another appointed date on God’s calendar that only He knows. It is that great day when Jesus will return and end all life and time on this earth. Maybe that day will come while you and I are still here. Maybe it will come next week. How prepared are you at all times for your appointment with God?

Jesus said, Therefore be ye also ready: for in such an hour as ye think not the Son of man cometh –Mat 24:44. Your appointment with God will happen when you’re not thinking about it.

A Prepared Place

Only prepared people will be rewarded with this perfect eternal place of peace and rest that Jesus is preparing. Heaven is a holy and prepared place for only holy and prepared people. Try to imagine how it would be if everything evil and rotten would be non-existent. No rust. No decay. No pain. No aging. No darkness. No sin. Read Revelation 21 and 22 for graphic descriptions of this prepared place—Heaven! The Bible says that there will be no more curse. Can you imagine a place with no more curse? Living in a place that is ravaged by the curse, we know of nothing different. All creation travails under the curse that man’s sin in the garden brought on us. But at the end of this life, God will reverse this curse! Think of it—death will be stopped. Chaos will be brought back to order. There will be no hunger, no thirst, no need of sun, no night, no sorrow, no crying, no pain, no tears. The pain and struggle that sin brought to this earth will simply BE NO MORE!

Heaven will be filled with the fulness of God’s glory. Those who prepared and won this race will be in the very presence of God—they will be like Him! Beloved, now are we the sons of God, and it doth not yet appear what we shall be: but we know that, when he shall appear, we shall be like him; for we shall see him as he is –1Jn 3:2.

Just as the physical sun sustains life on earth, so Jesus, the Son of God will sustain life in Heaven. He will be the source of everything needed to live in heaven—He will be the source and sustainer of life and hope for all eternity. But while the redeemed are enjoying the fulness of God in heaven, those in hell will be experiencing the complete opposite, most of all will be the absence of God.

Hell is the absence of God and all His attributes. No light—only pitch-black darkness. No bottom of gravity—only falling. No seasons—only intense heat. No rest—only constant gnashing of teeth and screaming. No water—only parched dry mouths. Nothing beautiful—only flames. No love—only hatred for the devil and his angels. No joy—only sorrow. No healing—only pain, pain, pain. No hope—only an eternal future of torment and regret. The curse in its fullest—with no restraints and no reverse!

What Will Your Last Words Be?

Ponder these last words of people who rejected Christ’s sacrifice:

Adams, an infidel said, “I’m lost, lost, lost. I am damned forever.” His agony was so great that as he died, he tore the hair from his head.

On his deathbed, Sir Julian Huxley, an English evolutionist, biologist, and staunch atheist said, “So it is true after all, so it is true after all.”

Cesare Borgia was a famous writer and politician who was a meticulous planner and planned everything to the minutest detail. When he knew he was dying he said, “When I lived, I provided for everything except death. Now I must die, and I am totally unprepared and unprovided.”

But the final words of the unbeliever are vastly different from those who believe in Jesus Christ. When Christians die, they often report, on their death bed, of seeing angels. Quite often they hear the most beautiful singing they’ve ever heard. The closer to death, the more beautiful the sound.

Charles Spurgeon said on his deathbed: “I can hear them coming!” He sat straight up in bed and asked: “Don’t you hear them? This is my coronation day. I can see the chariots, I’m ready to board.”

The final words of Augustus Toplady, author of the song Rock of Ages were, “All is light, light, light.”

Dwight L. Moody, a famous preacher, while on his deathbed said, “Can this be death? Why, it is better than living! Earth is receding, heaven is opening. This is my coronation day.”

What will your last words be on this earth? Are you daily preparing for eternity—your real home? Are you running as if your life depended on it? Your eternal destiny does.

Daar was ’n tyd in my lewe toe ek as vrywilliger by twee plaaslike EMS-stasies in Pennsilvanië, waar ek gewoon het, op die ambulansdiens gewerk het. Ek was ’n opgeleide EMT en toegerus om iemand wat seergekry het, te help.

Gedurende my dienstye was ek gereed om op ’n oomblik se kennisgewing aan die hardloop te spring. Ek het geen idee gehad wanneer my altyd-aanwesige pager alarm sou maak nie. Snags het ek ten volle geklee in my EMT-uitrusting geslaap. My stewels het by die deur gestaan. My motor was met sy agterkant na die huis geparkeer en die sleutels het op die bedkassie gelê. Ek was gereed!

Sommige nagte het my pager nooit afgegaan nie. Ander nagte het die pager hard gepiep en my uit ’n diep slaap geruk. Al die tyd wat ek aan voorbereiding bestee het, het vrugte afgewerp, en binne sekondes ná die alarm was ek op pad. Elke sekonde het getel. Ek moes te alle tye gereed wees.

Dit is geen geheim dat atlete wat aan die Olimpiese Spele deelneem, dikwels die grootste deel van hul lewe daaraan wy om vir die kompetisie voor te berei nie. Hulle wil niks liewer hê as om die doel te bereik om daardie medalje te wen nie. Maar hulle moet voorberei! Hulle word nie een oggend wakker en besluit om daardie dag na die Olimpiese Spele te reis om om die goue medalje mee te ding nie. As hulle wil wen, moet hulle voorberei. As hulle daardie goue medalje wil verower, moet hulle oefen.

Teen ongeveer die ouderdom van 14 het ’n Britse atleet reeds besluit op watter sportsoort om te fokus. Op daardie punt begin hy sy lewe aan opleiding wy. ’n Ongelooflike mate van toewyding, hulpbronne en belegging is nodig om op die hoogste vlak mee te ding. Die gemiddelde elite-atleet oefen ses uur per dag, ses dae per week, twaalf maande per jaar. Sy doel? Om te wen!

Een atleet het gesê: “Al die harde werk sal egter die moeite werd wees om bloot voor ’n tuisskare mee te ding—en om ’n medalje te wen, sal ’n droom wees wat waar word.”

As ’n Koninkryks-Christen kyk ek na so ’n aanhaling en sê: “Hoe ligsinnig en leeg.” Maar ek vra jou, jongmens: as hulle alles gee wat hulle het om iets so tydeliks te wen, wat gee jy om iets so ewig te wen? Wat gee jy vir ’n beloning wat enigiets op hierdie aarde sal oorleef—’n beloning waarvan die waarde buite hierdie wêreld lê?

Paulus het ’n hardloper gebruik as voorbeeld van hoe ons in ons Christelike lewe moet hardloop: Weet julle nie dat dié wat in ’n wedloop hardloop, wel almal hardloop, maar dat net een die prys ontvang nie? Hardloop só dat julle dit kan verkry –1Co 9:24. Jy moet hierdie wedloop van die Christelike lewe só hardloop dat jy kan wen! Ek vra jou: berei jy jou voor om te wen? Hardloop jy só dat jy sal wen?

Kom ons kyk kortliks na twee waarnemings oor ’n Olimpiese atleet en pas dit dan prakties op ons geestelike wandel toe.

Waarneming #1: ’n Atleet moet elke dag oefen.

Professionele atlete oefen nie omdat hulle moet nie. Hulle word groot met die vurige begeerte om die res van hul lewe hul sport te beoefen. Maar om dit te kan doen, weet hulle dat dit noodsaaklik is om oefening deel van die alledaagse lewe te maak as hulle wil wen. Dit maak nie saak of hulle hardloop, gewigte optel of gaan stap nie; atlete wat oefen, ontwikkel die gewoonte om daagliks te oefen. Dit is net so ’n deel van hul dag soos om hul tande te borsel of hul hare te kam.

En elkeen wat aan ’n wedstryd deelneem, onthou hom in alles. Hulle doen dit om ’n verganklike kroon te verkry, maar ons ’n onverganklike –1Co 9:25. As Christen, as jou doel is om tot die einde toe getrou te wees en die wedloop van jou Christelike lewe te wen, sal jy jou geestelike oefeninge ernstig moet opneem. Trouens, daaglikse geestelike oefeninge is noodsaaklik om fiks te bly vir hierdie uitmergelende wedloop.

’n Christen moet elke dag oefen. Lees jou Bybel asof jou lewe daarvan afhang—want dit doen! Bid en bly met dieselfde doelgerigtheid van hart met Jesus verbonde as waarmee ’n atleet vloeistof drink. (Het jy geweet dat vloeistof drink die belangrikste deel van ’n atleet se dieet is?) Bid asof jou lewe daarvan afhang—want dit doen!

Waarneming #2: ’n Atleet wat oefen, behaal die resultate wat hy verdien.

Dit is so moeilik om vroegoggend op te staan wanneer jy lekker onder die komberse lê en dit buite donker en koud is. Maar ’n atleet wat oefen, weet dat hy sal verloor as hy nie opstaan om te oefen nie. Hy weet dat hoe meer hy oefen, hoe groter is sy kans om te wen. ’n Atleet wat oefen, weet dat hy beloon sal word vir die tyd wat hy aan voorbereiding bestee. Om te kies om te oefen, sal resultate oplewer.

Sodat die reg van die wet in ons vervul kan word, in ons wat nie na die vlees wandel nie, maar na die Gees. Want dié wat volgens die vlees is, bedink die dinge van die vlees; maar dié wat volgens die Gees is, bedink die dinge van die Gees. Want om vleeslik te bedink, is die dood; maar om geestelik te bedink, is lewe en vrede –Rom 8: 4-6.

As Christen sal dit wat jy voed, groei. Jy sal óf die vlees voed, óf jy sal die Gees voed. As jy die wedloop wil wen en die beloning wil ontvang om herstel te word tot hoe jy werklik bedoel was om te lewe, sal jy geestelik moet wees en die dinge van die Gees moet voed. Kom ons kyk nou na ’n gedeeltelike lys van dinge wat, afhangend van hoe of waarom ons dit doen, sal bepaal of ons ons vlees of die Gees voed.

Om te jag en vleis vir die vrieskas te kry, is ’n baie natuurlike bedrywigheid wat nodig is vir oorlewing en wat al eeue lank gedoen word. Maar wanneer jy gaan jag om die grootste bok te skiet en jou ego en selfbeeld ’n hupstoot te gee, voed jy jou vlees.

Om na die wêreld se musiek te luister, sal niks doen om die geestelike mens te voed en te oefen nie. Maar jou vlees sal ryklik gevoed word.

Om die professionele sportwêreld te volg en/of daaraan deel te neem, sal jou nie help om die geestelike wedloop te wen nie. Trouens, jy sal verloor as jy jou vlees onnadenkend voed.

Vraatsug en/of die inname van ongesonde kos en drank sal nie jou geestelike mens help om in die Here te groei nie. Trouens, dit sal net jou begeerte na al hoe meer voed. Laat ons versigtig wees dat ons, of ons eet of drink, dit tot eer van God doen.

My liewe vriend, die eenvoudige feit bly staan: as jy nie volhard om jou geestelike lewe te dissiplineer nie, sal jy verloor! Wat oefen en voed jy dan—jou vlees of die Gees? Onthou, wanneer die natuurlike mens groei, is daar nie meer ruimte vir die geestelike mens om te groei nie.

Strek vorentoe en beur vorentoe

Paulus sê: Broeders, ek meen nie dat ek dit al verkry het nie; maar een ding doen ek: ek vergeet die dinge wat agter is en strek my uit na die dinge wat voor is, en beur vorentoe na die doel om die prys te verkry van die hoë roeping van God in Christus Jesus –Php 3:13-14.

Daar moet in jou Christelike lewe ’n beur en ’n uitstrek wees as jy wil wen. Jy kom nie net weg met die minimum doen in die Christelike lewe nie—God noem dit louheid, en die Bybel sê dat Hy ’n lou mens uit sy mond sal uitspoeg (sien Op. 3:16). God soek nie halfhartige oorwinnaars nie. Hy soek mense wat ‘meer as oorwinnaars’ is. Daar is geen plek vir louheid in die koninkryk van God nie!

Om onsself voor te berei om hierdie wedloop te wen, kan ons nie klaarkom sonder dissipline en selfopoffering nie. Is jy ’n gedissiplineerde mens in jou geestelike lewe? Hoe vergelyk dit met jou fisieke werk en stokperdjies? Staan jy vroeg op vir ’n fisieke sportsoort waarvan jy hou? Sorg jy dat jy betyds by jou werk is?

Het jy dieselfde dryfkrag om vroeg op te staan en jouself in jou geestelike lewe te dissiplineer? Gryp jy net so gretig na jou Bybel as na jou sagtebalkolfhandskoen? Gryp jy net so gretig na jou Bybel as na daardie blikkie koeldrank? Gryp jy net so gretig na jou Bybel as na jou geweer of boog om te gaan jag? Gryp jy net so gretig na jou Bybel as na jou foon? Bestee jy meer tyd daaraan om op jou geestelike lewe te fokus as om jouself aan te trek en jou hare te kam? Gee jy meer om vir wat jou vriende dink of vir wat Jesus dink?

Daar is ’n groot gier op sosiale media om vir almal te wys wat jy doen en die goedkeuring van mense te verkry. Om plasings op sosiale media te bekyk, sal jou van jou geestelike fokus beroof. Om op sosiale media-webwerwe te plaas sodat almal dit kan sien, voed ’n hunkering na mense se goedkeuring.

Daar is baie sosiale media-webwerwe en toepassings. Daar is egter een toepassing wat soortgelyke hunkeringe skep, maar op ’n subtieler manier. Dit is ’n toepassing waarmee jy vir ander kan vertel “wat aangaan”. Die toepassing se naam is WhatsApp. Hierdie toepassing is baie nuttig om boodskappe te stuur, veral aan kennisse wat oorsee is. Maar WhatsApp het ook ’n knoppie met die naam Status. Dit laat jou toe om dinge te plaas sodat ander dit kan sien. Dit laat jou toe om te sien wat jou vriende op die oomblik doen—wat hul status is!

Om jou bedrywighede en lewensgebeure aanlyn te plaas sodat die wêreld dit kan sien, het ’n allesoorheersende drang geword—’n hunkering na aandag en na mense se goedkeuring. As jy hierdie drang voed, sal dit groei. Vra jouself hierdie vrae: “Bring dit eer aan God wanneer ek my status op WhatsApp plaas? Bring dit my nader aan God wanneer ek sosiale media-webwerwe nagaan om te sien wat ander doen en hoe hulle aangetrek is? Is ek gretiger om my vriende se status na te gaan as om my Bybel oop te maak en die stand van my wandel met God na te gaan?” Maak die tyd wat jy op jou foon deurbring jou beter voorbereid om hierdie wedloop te wen?

Die aanspraak op jou tyd

Hoeveel tyd bestee jy aan oefening? As ’n atleet een opstoot per dag doen, dink jy hy sal wen? As ’n atleet wat desperaat daardie goue medalje wil wen, elke dag net 1/10 myl sou stap, dink jy hy sal wen?

As jy jou dus voorberei om God te ontmoet en hierdie wedloop te wen, is een Bybelvers per dag genoeg om te wen? Is een minuut se gebedstyd elke dag saam met jou Verlosser genoeg om die hewige geestelike stryd met die vyand te voer?

Neem tyd om jou Bybel te lees—jou lewe hang daarvan af om te oorleef! Neem tyd om te bid—jy kan nie hierdie wedloop sonder gebed hardloop nie!

“Ek het een oggend vroeg opgestaan en my
reguit in die dag gehaas;
Ek het soveel gehad om te doen dat ek nie
tyd gehad het om te bid nie.
Probleme het my van alle kante oorval, en
elke taak het al swaarder geword;
“Waarom help God my nie?” het ek gewonder.
Hy het geantwoord: “Jy het nie gevra nie.”
Ek wou vreugde en skoonheid sien, maar die dag
het grys en somber voortgesloer;
Ek het gewonder waarom God dit nie vir my wys nie. Hy
het gesê: “Maar jy het nie gesoek nie.”
Ek het probeer om in God se teenwoordigheid te kom; ek het
al my sleutels in die slot probeer.
God het my sag en liefdevol tereggewys: “My
kind, jy het nie geklop nie.”
Ek het vanoggend vroeg wakker geword en stilgestaan
voordat ek die dag ingegaan het;
Ek het soveel gehad om te doen dat ek
tyd moes maak om te bid.”
-anoniem

Die aanspraak op ons tyd kan nie groter wees nie. Tegnologiese geriewe vorm ons lewens. Ons bloeiende ekonomie eis ons tyd op. Ons leef in geestelik gevaarlike tye! Het die eise en afleidings van die lewe die tyd wat jy aan geestelike oefening bestee, verminder? Pla dit jou wanneer die tyd wat jy aan gebed en Bybellees bestee, afneem omdat jy eenvoudig nie tyd het nie?

Verwyder afleidings

Daarom dan, terwyl ons ook so ’n groot wolk van getuies rondom ons het, laat ons elke las aflê en die sonde wat ons so maklik verstrik, en laat ons met volharding die wedloop hardloop wat voor ons lê, –Heb 12:1.

Die Griekse woord vir las beskryf dit as ’n hindernis. Is daar bedrywighede of gewoontes wat jou verhinder om alles te gee om hierdie wedloop te hardloop? Is daar iets wat jou oefening—jou geestelike groei—belemmer?

Die Griekse woord vir verstrik beskryf dit as om af te lei of mee te ding. Is daar sondes wat jou van die wedloop aflei? Is daar dinge wat jy doen wat met jou geestelike oefeninge meeding?

Miskien is besigwees die las wat jou wedloop belemmer. Miskien is geestelike traagheid jou sonde—traagheid is ’n gebrek aan belangstelling of besorgdheid. Jy het geestelik aan die slaap geraak, en jy gee eenvoudig nie om nie. Miskien ding dinge wat die wêreld hoog aanslaan met jou geestelike lewe en oefening mee—dinge soos rykdom, sport en gewildheid. Die wêreld heg groot waarde aan klere. Het jy al inkopies gedoen en ’n kledingstuk gekoop wat jy nie regtig nodig gehad het nie, net omdat dit mooi was—’n nuwe styl?

Miskien is jou las of afleiding bloot ’n gebrek aan ’n visie vir die koninkryk van God. Die Bybel sê dat waar daar geen visie is nie, die volk te gronde gaan. As jy nie ’n visie het nie, sal jy te gronde gaan. Eenvoudig gestel, jy sal die wedloop verloor en hel toe gaan as jy nie ’n visie vir die Koninkryk van God het nie!

Ek moedig jou aan om jou lewe voor die Here oop te lê—vra Hom hierdie ernstige vrae.

  • “God, is my prioriteite reg?”
  • “God, heg ek waarde aan wat U waardevol ag?”
  • “God, ontbreek dit my aan visie?”
  • “God, strek ek my uit na dinge wat nie hou nie?”
  • “God, is ek te besig om agter dinge aan te hardloop wat my hardloop belemmer?”
  • “God, wat is my las—wat is my hindernis?”

Dit gaan alles daaroor om voor te berei om die Here te ontmoet en vir ons ewige bestemming voor te berei. Dit gaan alles daaroor om doeltreffende soldate in Sy koninkryk te wees. As jy weier om hier op aarde die wedloop goed te hardloop en getrou te wees, dink jy God wil jou in die hemel hê?

Miskien moet jy desperaat voor God raak. Miskien moet jy ingrypende veranderinge in jou lewe aanbring—veranderinge aan jou skedule, jou fokus, jou bedrywighede en jou strewes.

Geen mens ken die tyd nie

Ons almal het ’n vasgestelde sterftyd op God se kalender. Jy het geen idee op watter dag van watter jaar jou naam op God se kalender staan nie. Dit kan wees dat jy nog net een week op hierdie aarde oor het.

Daar is ook nog ’n vasgestelde datum op God se kalender wat net Hy ken. Dit is daardie groot dag wanneer Jesus sal terugkeer en alle lewe en tyd op hierdie aarde tot ’n einde sal bring. Miskien sal daardie dag kom terwyl ek en jy nog hier is. Miskien kom dit volgende week. Hoe gereed is jy te alle tye vir jou afspraak met God?

Jesus het gesê: Daarom moet julle ook gereed wees, want die Seun van die mens kom op ’n uur wanneer julle dit nie verwag nie –Mat 24:44. Jou afspraak met God sal plaasvind wanneer jy nie daaraan dink nie.

’n Plek wat voorberei is

Slegs diegene wat voorberei is, sal beloon word met hierdie volmaakte ewige plek van vrede en rus wat Jesus voorberei. Die hemel is ’n heilige en voorbereide plek, net vir heilige en voorbereide mense. Probeer jou indink hoe dit sou wees as alles wat boos en sleg is, nie sou bestaan nie. Geen roes nie. Geen verval nie. Geen pyn nie. Geen veroudering nie. Geen duisternis nie. Geen sonde nie. Lees Openbaring 21 en 22 vir grafiese beskrywings van hierdie voorbereide plek—die hemel! Die Bybel sê dat daar geen vloek meer sal wees nie. Kan jy jou ’n plek voorstel waar daar geen vloek meer is nie? Omdat ons in ’n plek woon wat deur die vloek geteister word, ken ons niks anders nie. Die hele skepping sug onder die vloek wat die mens se sonde in die tuin oor ons gebring het. Maar aan die einde van hierdie lewe sal God hierdie vloek omkeer! Dink net daaraan—die dood sal tot stilstand gebring word. Chaos sal weer orde word. Daar sal geen honger, geen dors, geen behoefte aan die son, geen nag, geen droefheid, geen geween, geen pyn en geen trane wees nie. Die pyn en stryd wat sonde na hierdie aarde gebring het, sal eenvoudig NIE MEER WEES NIE!

Die hemel sal vol wees van die volheid van God se heerlikheid. Diegene wat hulle voorberei het en hierdie wedloop gewen het, sal in God se teenwoordigheid wees—hulle sal soos Hy wees! Geliefdes, nou is ons kinders van God, en dit is nog nie geopenbaar wat ons sal wees nie; maar ons weet dat wanneer Hy verskyn, ons soos Hy sal wees, omdat ons Hom sal sien soos Hy is –1Jn 3:2.

Net soos die fisiese son lewe op aarde onderhou, sal Jesus, die Seun van God, lewe in die hemel onderhou. Hy sal die bron wees van alles wat nodig is om in die hemel te lewe—Hy sal vir ewig die bron en onderhouer van lewe en hoop wees. Maar terwyl die verlostes die volheid van God in die hemel geniet, sal dié in die hel die volslae teenoorgestelde ervaar; bo alles sal God afwesig wees.

Die hel is die afwesigheid van God en al sy eienskappe. Geen lig nie—net pikswart duisternis. Geen swaartekragbodem nie—net val. Geen seisoene nie—net intense hitte. Geen rus nie—net gedurige tandeknersing en geskreeu. Geen water nie—net kurkdroë monde. Niks mooi nie—net vlamme. Geen liefde nie—net haat vir die duiwel en sy engele. Geen vreugde nie—net droefheid. Geen genesing nie—net pyn, pyn, pyn. Geen hoop nie—net ’n ewige toekoms van foltering en berou. Die vloek in sy volle omvang—sonder beperking en sonder omkeer!

Wat sal jou laaste woorde wees?

Dink na oor hierdie laaste woorde van mense wat Christus se offer verwerp het:

Adams, ’n ongelowige, het gesê: “Ek is verlore, verlore, verlore. Ek is vir ewig verdoem.” Sy angs was so groot dat hy, terwyl hy sterwend was, die hare van sy kop uitgeruk het.

Op sy sterfbed het sir Julian Huxley, ’n Engelse evolusionis, bioloog en uitgesproke ateïs, gesê: “Dit is dus tog waar, dit is dus tog waar.”

Cesare Borgia was ’n bekende skrywer en politikus, ’n noukeurige beplanner wat alles tot in die fynste besonderhede beplan het. Toe hy besef dat hy sterwend was, het hy gesê: “Toe ek gelewe het, het ek vir alles voorsiening gemaak behalwe die dood. Nou moet ek sterf, en ek is heeltemal onvoorbereid en het niks gereël nie.”

Maar die laaste woorde van die ongelowige verskil hemelsbreed van dié van mense wat in Jesus Christus glo. Wanneer Christene sterf, vertel hulle dikwels op hul sterfbed dat hulle engele sien. Heel dikwels hoor hulle die mooiste sang wat hulle nog ooit gehoor het. Hoe nader die dood kom, hoe mooier klink dit.

Charles Spurgeon het op sy sterfbed gesê: “Ek kan hulle hoor kom!” Hy het regop in die bed gaan sit en gevra: “Hoor julle hulle nie? Dit is my kroningsdag. Ek kan die strydwaens sien; ek is gereed om in te klim.”

Die laaste woorde van Augustus Toplady, skrywer van die lied Rock of Ages, was: “Alles is lig, lig, lig.”

Dwight L. Moody, ’n bekende prediker, het op sy sterfbed gesê: “Kan dit die dood wees? Wel, dit is beter as om te lewe! Die aarde wyk, die hemel gaan oop. Dit is my kroningsdag.”

Wat sal jou laaste woorde op hierdie aarde wees? Berei jy jou daagliks voor vir die ewigheid—jou ware tuiste? Hardloop jy asof jou lewe daarvan afhang? Jou ewige bestemming doen.

Who would have ever imagined that a little germ which cannot be seen with the human eye, has put the entire globe in a tizzy, a panic, and an economic disruption? I have not seen a pandemic of this magnitude in my lifetime and, when this first emerged, I was one of the gainsayers who could not believe it would cripple our world to this extent. Questions abound, conspiracy theories are propagated, and fear has run rampant throughout the world as the entire globe responds to the pandemic. Will there be a cure, or will this continue to be a scourge in our world? If this little virus trespasses into my physical body, what is the chance of survival? Will it affect any of my loved ones? The questions are innumerable. Where it has come from has been theorized by many, but does anyone really know? Where is God in the whole thing? Did it surprise Him? Is it God’s judgment on humanity? These and many other questions are being asked by many sincere people and the answers that are given often contradict one another.

One of the outfalls of the pandemic is the government invasion into the church and our personal lives in a way that has been unprecedented in my and your lifetime. Suddenly, we are faced with decisions that many of us have not thought through. When, and how much, should the government mandate things in our lives when we clearly believe in separation of Church and state? What are my rights? What will I do if I lose my business? Will I cash in the stimulus check that is supposed to arrive in the mail in the near future?

There is a verse in Peter that reminds me that if anyone should have answers in this time of pandemic, we as Christians should. But sanctify the Lord God in your hearts: and be ready always to give an answer to every man that asketh you a reason of the hope that is in you with meekness and fear: –1Pe 3:15. We may not know the origin of the virus, nor the outcome, but we do know Who knows all things, and that it was not a surprise to Him. It is the right time to turn to the Lord Jesus Christ, the One who holds all things by the power of His Word. If anytime in recent history the Christian has an opportunity to be salt in the earth and light in the world, it is during this time of upheaval. So, what should the response of the Christian be?

Consider this verse in Luke: Men’s hearts failing them for fear, and for looking after those things which are coming on the earth… –Luk 21:26. For the Christian, earthquakes, famines, and pestilence should be no surprise since they have been prophesied to us through the Word of God. And while these things are happening and will happen, God has provided clear scriptural mandates for us as Christians to follow. We are clearly commanded in the scripture to not worry about tomorrow: Take therefore no thought for the morrow: for the morrow shall take thought for the things of itself. Sufficient unto the day is the evil thereof –Mat 6:34.

So, we as Jesus’ disciples know that God will give us wisdom and grace for the difficulties of today. We are commanded to not borrow tomorrow’s troubles. We need to be reminded once again, in this time, as always, God will provide grace for today that will be great enough to sustain peace in the midst of the storm, and will provide it tomorrow if we live. Let us learn a lesson from Peter and the disciples—to focus on Jesus. We need to trust Jesus even when He seems to be asleep in the boat, rather than focusing on the storm that is raging all around us. Jesus was in control whether he was sleeping or awake and still is. But we might say, “How do I know if I will have food or clothing, or my business tomorrow?” And again, we hear the Savior say, “Look at the lilies, the fowls of the air, and learn a lesson from them!” We cannot even do some of the simplest things by God’s estimation, like add a cubit to our stature, so why would we try to deal with the hard things of providing for a tomorrow that is out of our control? Do these commands fit for the year 2020 and the pandemic that we are facing? I am sure that, in theory, we can agree, but can we internalize these verses and make them a very prominent place in our lives today?

There are principles given in God’s Word that, if we have not embraced them, we will also ‘reel in a tizzy’ when faced with things like the pandemic that is completely out of our control. One of those principles is the clear teaching that suffering is a way of life for the follower of Jesus. And if children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ; if so be that we suffer with him, that we may be also glorified together –Rom 8:17.

The ‘health and wealth’ gospel that is peddled by many preachers today is a false doctrine and can leave a person reeling when they are faced with health or economic loss. We need to be okay with suffering, we need to embrace it; we need to arm ourselves with the same mind as Christ. The loss of our business, home and yes, even our own lives also, by economic disaster, storms, or accidents is not outside the realm of the will of God for the Christian. We know that God can eliminate any of these calamities and will protect us from them all IF He so wills. But whether He does or not is God’s prerogative and we are the happiest IF we surrender our lives completely to Him in faith, and trust Him to keep us, whether with little or with much.

Another principle we need to reckon with is that we have no rights except the right to the Tree of Life. For us as Christians it makes little difference if we are citizens of the United States or not. We have many privileges for which we are very grateful for, but we should not think we have a right to own, keep, or buy, or that we have a stake to claim in this world. In the Holy Scriptures we are reminded that we are but pilgrims and strangers here (see Heb 11:13-16). As Abraham and the other patriarchs, we have no abiding city here but look for a city …whose builder and maker is God –Heb 11:10.

There are plenty of lawyers offering to fight for our rights, but the truth of the matter is, our citizenship is in Heaven and we are just ambassadors here and can be kicked out by society and need to leave all anytime without a moment’s hesitation. If this will be a reality, we need to live our lives with all our things held with an open hand. We do not have the right (only the privilege)—to own land, to have enough food, to enjoy good health, and to live without suffering—nor should we fight for those so-called rights, but we, God’s people, must put on the mind of Christ and be willing to leave all behind for the sake of Christ and trust Him completely for our sustenance. Jesus said He sees one sparrow fall to the ground and reminds us that we are worth more than many sparrows. Jesus calls us to hate all that we hold dear here on this earth: If any man come to me, and hate not his father, and mother, and wife, and children, and brethren, and sisters, yea, and his own life also, he cannot be my disciple –Luk 14:26.

As Christians, we do not plan to stay here on this earth; we are anticipating Heaven. The scriptures express this sentiment when it not only considers the whole earth groaning to be delivered from this death and decay, but that we ourselves are also groaning to be delivered. Should there be such a strong pull to be here that our hearts fail us …for fear, and for looking after those things which are coming on the earth…? –Luk 21:26. Should we much rather cry out “how long Lord Jesus” “so come”? Even as the apostle intimates as he wrestles with being “betwixt two”—For I am in a strait betwixt two, having a desire to depart, and to be with Christ; which is far better: Nevertheless to abide in the flesh is more needful for you. –Php 1:23-24. The apostle clearly indicates “having a desire to depart and be with Christ is far better,” and the only thing that holds him here is the fact that there is work to be done.

Another area we should be awake to, is our vulnerability during this time of no church services. We may be tempted to go on-line and be fed spiritually by those who are false prophets or those who teach false doctrine. We need to “try the spirits” and know whose feet we are sitting at. Be selective to whom you might listen, or from whom you might allow your family to take nourishment. We, as fathers, are called to lead and lead we must. The burden is on our shoulders to help our families navigate through these uncertain times. We as fathers may need to be more proactive during this time. It is a call to us to rise up and lead our wives and children. Not only do we have to watch “whose feet we are sitting at”, but we need to lead our families with confidence, calling them to trust in God, and leading them in prayers of faith. We need to provide them with an example of faith and trust in God that no amount of buffeting will shake. This time of upheaval will not knock us off our feet IF we are rooted and grounded in Christ.

At a time like this, we need to make wise decisions, even decisions concerning the future, but still refrain from falling into the panic mode and running around as if we have no Heavenly Father. We also need to lead our families in being careful not to believe everything that one hears, but to be aware of where our news is coming from and to consider how reliable it is. Conspiracy theories abound concerning how this virus started and the political agenda theorized to be behind it. Refrain from spending time following these conspirators and rather follow the scripture mandate, “casting down imaginations.” The simple truth is this, we do not know, and if we did know it still should not change the way we live and our overall response. God has not given us the spirit of fear, but of power, of love and a sound mind. John tells us to not “believe every spirit, but to try the spirits to see whether they be of God.”

I believe that this is an awesome opportunity to reach out to our fellow brothers and sisters by praying for one another and by staying in touch so that we can ‘weep with those that weep’ and ‘rejoice with those that rejoice’. Some of us have jobs and some do not. God’s Word tells us that those who have are to give to those who do not have so that there may be an equality. It is a time to reach out to the elderly in our church or community and stay in touch by mail or phone. This is a time in which the lonely will only get lonelier. A cheery word, or a letter in the mail, and whatever other resources you can appropriately use may be just the thing that those around you need.

During the times of mandatory “stay at home”, there is a whole group of our society that will face challenges that they have not seen up to this time. According to various news sources there has been an increase in domestic violence since family members are spending much more time together than they normally do. But let this not once be named among us. This is the time for us as God’s children to maximize on “in home” relationships. The Bible calls us to “redeem the time” and this can be done by making the most of our time together as a family. Spend time together—reading the Bible, praying together, singing together, and just simply doing enjoyable things together—things that will nurture growth and love in our relationships. We need to be creative as fathers in bringing our family together in a way that will produce an atmosphere of unity and oneness.

One question that begs an answer is this, “Should the government dictate whether we have church or not?” This is something we need to answer since for some areas of the country it is more than a suggestion but has become mandatory. I believe that since the suggestion/order to not meet together during this time is for the purpose of not spreading a virus that is quite contagious, this then fulfills the scripture “to love our neighbor as ourselves.” It is a good opportunity to show the public that if the mandate does not ask us to violate the scripture, then we choose to honor the government. There may come a time soon enough that we will be asked to do something that we cannot do with a clear conscience and then we will need to stand and “obey God rather than men.”

Some feel a twang of guilt because of the verse, “to not forsake the assembling of ourselves together”, however, this seems to be addressing a habit or a way of life. I suppose this is dealing with the lazy, slothful heart that does not see the benefit of getting together. We want to get together… As soon as we can get together again, we will take advantage of it. There is a big difference between those who cannot get together for a short time and those that choose not to since they do not see the value of it. For the present time, it seems the best testimony to our world and public relations to honor the mandate since they are not fighting against our faith and God. Let’s just take care to not let this become our new normal. Let’s keep our eye on a path forward to once again practically function as a local body.

What can we do? Pray more than ever that God would use this to win the lost and refine the church. Spend time building relationships with those you are closest to and have been encouraged to stay home with. Let this pandemic prepare us for what God has for us in the future. Let us be very careful how we talk about the government and some of the rulings that have come out through this all. We are called to honor the king and we need to spend more time thanking God for our freedoms than maximizing on the negative—I exhort therefore, that, first of all, supplications, prayers, intercessions, and giving of thanks, be made for all men; For kings, and for all that are in authority; that we may lead a quiet and peaceable life in all godliness and honesty. For this is good and acceptable in the sight of God our Saviour; –1Ti 2:1-3. For the Christian, …we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose –Rom 8:28.

Wer hätte je gedacht, dass ein winziger Keim, den man mit bloßem Auge nicht sehen kann, den ganzen Erdball in Aufruhr und Panik versetzen und eine wirtschaftliche Krise auslösen würde? In meinem Leben habe ich noch keine Pandemie dieses Ausmaßes erlebt, und als sie zum ersten Mal auftrat, gehörte ich zu denen, die nicht glauben konnten, dass sie unsere Welt derart lähmen würde. Es gibt viele Fragen, Verschwörungstheorien werden verbreitet, und die Angst hat sich auf der ganzen Welt ausgebreitet, während der gesamte Erdball auf die Pandemie reagiert. Wird es ein Heilmittel geben, oder wird dies weiterhin eine Plage in unserer Welt sein? Wie groß ist die Überlebenschance, wenn dieses kleine Virus in meinen Körper eindringt? Wird es jemanden treffen, den ich liebe? Die Fragen sind unzählig. Viele haben darüber spekuliert, woher es gekommen ist, aber weiß es wirklich jemand? Wo ist Gott in all dem? Hat es Ihn überrascht? Ist es Gottes Gericht über die Menschheit? Viele aufrichtige Menschen stellen diese und zahlreiche weitere Fragen, und die gegebenen Antworten widersprechen sich oft.

Eine der Folgen der Pandemie ist, dass die Regierung in einer Weise in die Kirche und unser persönliches Leben eingreift, wie es zu unseren Lebzeiten noch nie dagewesen ist. Plötzlich stehen wir vor Entscheidungen, über die viele von uns noch nicht gründlich nachgedacht haben. Wann und in welchem Ausmaß sollte die Regierung Dinge in unserem Leben anordnen, wenn wir doch eindeutig an die Trennung von Kirche und Staat glauben? Welche Rechte habe ich? Was werde ich tun, wenn ich mein Geschäft verliere? Werde ich den Konjunkturscheck einlösen, der in naher Zukunft per Post eintreffen soll?

Ein Vers im Petrusbrief erinnert mich daran, dass wir als Christen Antworten haben sollten, wenn überhaupt jemand in dieser Pandemiezeit Antworten haben sollte. Heiligt aber den Herrn Christus in euren Herzen. Seid jederzeit bereit, jedem Rede und Antwort zu stehen, der euch nach der Hoffnung fragt, die in euch ist, doch mit Sanftmut und Ehrfurcht: –1. Petrus 3:15. Vielleicht kennen wir weder den Ursprung des Virus noch den Ausgang, aber wir wissen, wer alles weiß und dass es für Ihn keine Überraschung war. Jetzt ist der richtige Zeitpunkt, sich dem Herrn Jesus Christus zuzuwenden, der alles durch die Macht seines Wortes erhält. Wenn Christen in der jüngeren Geschichte je Gelegenheit hatten, Salz der Erde und Licht der Welt zu sein, dann in dieser Zeit des Umbruchs. Wie sollte ein Christ also reagieren?

Denkt an diesen Vers im Lukasevangelium: Die Menschen werden vor Angst vergehen und in Erwartung dessen, was über die Erde kommen wird … –Lukas 21:26. Für Christen sollten Erdbeben, Hungersnöte und Seuchen keine Überraschung sein, denn sie sind uns durch das Wort Gottes vorausgesagt worden. Und während diese Dinge geschehen und auch künftig geschehen werden, hat Gott uns als Christen klare biblische Gebote gegeben, denen wir folgen sollen. In der Schrift wird uns eindeutig geboten, uns nicht um den morgigen Tag zu sorgen: Sorgt euch also nicht um den morgigen Tag; denn der morgige Tag wird für das Seine sorgen. Jeder Tag hat genug an seiner eigenen Plage. –Matthäus 6:34.

Wir als Jünger Jesu wissen also, dass Gott uns Weisheit und Gnade für die Schwierigkeiten des heutigen Tages geben wird. Uns ist geboten, uns nicht die Sorgen von morgen aufzubürden. In dieser Zeit müssen wir uns wieder daran erinnern, dass Gott wie immer für den heutigen Tag Gnade geben wird, die groß genug ist, um uns mitten im Sturm Frieden zu schenken, und dass er sie morgen geben wird, wenn wir dann noch leben. Lernen wir von Petrus und den Jüngern, unseren Blick auf Jesus zu richten. Wir müssen Jesus vertrauen, selbst wenn er scheinbar im Boot schläft, statt auf den Sturm zu schauen, der um uns herum tobt. Jesus hatte die Kontrolle, ob er schlief oder wach war, und hat sie noch immer. Doch vielleicht sagen wir: „Woher soll ich wissen, ob ich morgen etwas zu essen oder Kleidung haben werde oder ob mein Geschäft noch besteht?“ Und wieder hören wir den Erlöser sagen: „Seht euch die Lilien und die Vögel des Himmels an und lernt von ihnen!“ Nach Gottes Maßstab können wir nicht einmal einige der einfachsten Dinge tun, etwa unserer Körpergröße eine Elle hinzufügen. Warum sollten wir also versuchen, uns um die schwierigen Dinge zu kümmern, die Versorgung für einen morgigen Tag zu sichern, der nicht in unserer Hand liegt? Gelten diese Gebote auch für das Jahr 2020 und die Pandemie, der wir gegenüberstehen? Ich bin sicher, dass wir ihnen theoretisch zustimmen können, aber können wir diese Verse verinnerlichen und ihnen heute einen ganz zentralen Platz in unserem Leben einräumen?

In Gottes Wort finden sich Grundsätze, die wir, wenn wir sie nicht angenommen haben, ebenfalls „in Aufruhr geraten“ lassen, wenn wir mit etwas wie der Pandemie konfrontiert sind, die völlig außerhalb unserer Kontrolle liegt. Einer dieser Grundsätze ist die klare Lehre, dass Leiden zum Leben eines Nachfolgers Jesu gehört. Wenn aber Kinder, dann auch Erben – Erben Gottes und Miterben Christi –, wenn wir wirklich mit ihm leiden, damit wir auch mit ihm verherrlicht werden. –Römer 8:17.

Das „Wohlstands- und Gesundheits-Evangelium“, das heute von vielen Predigern verbreitet wird, ist eine falsche Lehre und kann einen Menschen völlig aus der Bahn werfen, wenn er mit gesundheitlichen oder wirtschaftlichen Verlusten konfrontiert wird. Wir müssen mit dem Leiden zurechtkommen; wir müssen es annehmen und uns mit derselben Gesinnung wie Christus wappnen. Der Verlust unseres Geschäfts, unseres Hauses und ja, sogar unseres eigenen Lebens durch wirtschaftliche Katastrophen, Unwetter oder Unfälle liegt für Christen nicht außerhalb des Willens Gottes. Wir wissen, dass Gott jede dieser Notlagen abwenden und uns vor ihnen allen bewahren kann, WENN er es will. Ob er es aber tut oder nicht, steht Gott zu; am glücklichsten sind wir, WENN wir unser Leben ihm im Glauben ganz übergeben und darauf vertrauen, dass er für uns sorgt, ob wir wenig oder viel haben.

Ein weiterer Grundsatz, mit dem wir uns auseinandersetzen müssen, lautet, dass wir keine Rechte haben außer dem Recht auf den Baum des Lebens. Für uns als Christen macht es wenig aus, ob wir Bürger der Vereinigten Staaten sind oder nicht. Wir haben viele Privilegien, für die wir sehr dankbar sind, aber wir sollten nicht meinen, wir hätten ein Recht darauf, etwas zu besitzen, zu behalten oder zu kaufen oder einen Anspruch auf diese Welt zu erheben. In der Heiligen Schrift werden wir daran erinnert, dass wir hier nur Pilger und Fremde sind (siehe Hebräer 11:13-16). Wie Abraham und die anderen Erzväter haben wir hier keine bleibende Stadt, sondern warten auf eine Stadt … deren Baumeister und Schöpfer Gott ist. –Hebräer 11:10.

Es gibt viele Anwälte, die anbieten, für unsere Rechte zu kämpfen, aber tatsächlich ist unser Bürgerrecht im Himmel. Hier sind wir nur Gesandte und können von der Gesellschaft ausgewiesen werden; jederzeit müssen wir ohne das geringste Zögern alles verlassen können. Wenn dies Wirklichkeit werden kann, müssen wir so leben, dass wir an all unserem Besitz mit offener Hand festhalten. Wir haben kein Recht (sondern nur das Privileg), Land zu besitzen, genug zu essen zu haben, uns guter Gesundheit zu erfreuen und ohne Leiden zu leben – und wir sollten auch nicht für diese sogenannten Rechte kämpfen. Vielmehr müssen wir als Gottes Volk die Gesinnung Christi anziehen, bereit sein, um Christi willen alles zurückzulassen, und ihm für unseren Lebensunterhalt völlig vertrauen. Jesus sagte, dass er sieht, wenn ein Spatz zu Boden fällt, und erinnert uns daran, dass wir mehr wert sind als viele Spatzen. Jesus ruft uns dazu auf, alles zu hassen, was uns hier auf Erden lieb und teuer ist: Wenn jemand zu mir kommt und hasst nicht seinen Vater und seine Mutter, seine Frau und seine Kinder, seine Brüder und Schwestern, ja sogar sein eigenes Leben, der kann nicht mein Jünger sein. –Lukas 14:26.

Als Christen planen wir nicht, hier auf Erden zu bleiben; wir sehnen uns nach dem Himmel. Die Schrift bringt diesen Gedanken zum Ausdruck, indem sie nicht nur davon spricht, dass die ganze Erde seufzt und von diesem Tod und Verfall befreit werden möchte, sondern auch davon, dass wir selbst seufzen und befreit werden möchten. Sollte uns der Wunsch, hier zu bleiben, so stark gefangen nehmen, dass wir vor Angst vergehen und in Erwartung dessen, was über die Erde kommen wird …? –Lukas 21:26. Sollten wir nicht viel eher rufen: „Wie lange noch, Herr Jesus?“ und „Komm doch!“? So deutet es auch der Apostel an, während er mit dem Gedanken ringt, „zwischen zweien“ zu stehen: Denn ich werde von beidem bedrängt: Ich habe den Wunsch, aufzubrechen und bei Christus zu sein, denn das ist weit besser. Doch im Fleisch zu bleiben ist um euretwillen nötiger. –Philipper 1:23-24. Der Apostel macht deutlich: „Der Wunsch, aufzubrechen und bei Christus zu sein, ist weit besser“, und nur die Tatsache, dass noch Arbeit zu tun ist, hält ihn hier zurück.

Ein weiterer Bereich, für den wir in dieser Zeit ohne Gottesdienste wachsam sein sollten, ist unsere Verwundbarkeit. Wir könnten versucht sein, online zu gehen und uns geistlich von falschen Propheten oder solchen nähren zu lassen, die falsche Lehren verbreiten. Wir müssen „die Geister prüfen“ und wissen, zu wessen Füßen wir sitzen. Wählt sorgfältig aus, wem ihr zuhört und von wem ihr zulassen wollt, dass eure Familie geistliche Nahrung erhält. Wir Väter sind dazu berufen, die Führung zu übernehmen, und das müssen wir tun. Es liegt an uns, unseren Familien zu helfen, durch diese unsicheren Zeiten zu navigieren. In dieser Zeit müssen wir Väter vielleicht noch vorausschauender handeln. Wir sind aufgerufen, aufzustehen und unsere Frauen und Kinder zu führen. Wir müssen nicht nur darauf achten, „zu wessen Füßen wir sitzen“, sondern unsere Familien auch zuversichtlich führen, sie zum Vertrauen auf Gott aufrufen und sie in Gebeten des Glaubens anleiten. Wir müssen ihnen ein Beispiel für Glauben und Vertrauen auf Gott geben, das durch keinerlei Erschütterung ins Wanken gebracht wird. Diese Zeit des Umbruchs wird uns nicht von den Füßen reißen, WENN wir in Christus verwurzelt und gegründet sind.

In einer Zeit wie dieser müssen wir weise Entscheidungen treffen, auch Entscheidungen über die Zukunft, und uns dennoch davor hüten, in Panik zu verfallen und umherzurennen, als hätten wir keinen himmlischen Vater. Wir müssen unsere Familien auch dazu anleiten, nicht alles zu glauben, was man hört, sondern darauf zu achten, woher unsere Nachrichten stammen und wie zuverlässig sie sind. Über den Ursprung dieses Virus und die dahinter vermutete politische Agenda gibt es zahlreiche Verschwörungstheorien. Verbringt keine Zeit damit, diesen Verschwörungstheoretikern zu folgen; folgt lieber dem Gebot der Schrift: „Gedankengebilde niederreißen.“ Die einfache Wahrheit ist: Wir wissen es nicht, und selbst wenn wir es wüssten, dürfte das unsere Lebensweise und unsere grundsätzliche Reaktion nicht ändern. Gott hat uns nicht einen Geist der Furcht gegeben, sondern der Kraft, der Liebe und der Besonnenheit. Johannes sagt uns, wir sollen nicht „jedem Geist glauben, sondern die Geister prüfen, ob sie aus Gott sind“.

Ich glaube, dies ist eine wunderbare Gelegenheit, unseren Brüdern und Schwestern beizustehen, füreinander zu beten und miteinander in Kontakt zu bleiben, damit wir „mit den Weinenden weinen“ und „mit den Fröhlichen uns freuen“ können. Einige von uns haben Arbeit, andere nicht. Gottes Wort sagt uns, dass die, die haben, denen geben sollen, die nichts haben, damit ein Ausgleich entsteht. Es ist eine Zeit, den älteren Menschen in unserer Gemeinde oder Nachbarschaft die Hand zu reichen und per Post oder Telefon in Kontakt zu bleiben. In dieser Zeit werden Einsame noch einsamer. Ein freundliches Wort, ein Brief per Post oder andere Mittel, die ihr auf angemessene Weise nutzen könnt, sind vielleicht genau das, was die Menschen um euch herum brauchen.

Während der Zeiten verpflichtender „Bleibt zu Hause“-Anordnungen wird eine ganze Gruppe in unserer Gesellschaft vor Herausforderungen stehen, denen sie bisher nicht begegnet ist. Verschiedenen Nachrichtenquellen zufolge hat häusliche Gewalt zugenommen, weil Familienmitglieder viel mehr Zeit miteinander verbringen als sonst. Doch das soll unter uns nicht einmal erwähnt werden. Jetzt ist für uns als Kinder Gottes die Zeit, unsere Beziehungen zu Hause zu stärken. Die Bibel ruft uns dazu auf, „die Zeit auszukaufen“, und das können wir tun, indem wir unsere gemeinsame Zeit als Familie bestmöglich nutzen. Verbringt Zeit miteinander – lest die Bibel, betet gemeinsam, singt gemeinsam und unternehmt einfach Dinge, die euch Freude machen –, Dinge, die das Wachstum und die Liebe in unseren Beziehungen fördern. Wir Väter müssen kreativ sein und unsere Familien so zusammenbringen, dass eine Atmosphäre der Einheit und Verbundenheit entsteht.

Eine Frage, die nach einer Antwort verlangt, lautet: „Sollte die Regierung bestimmen, ob wir Gottesdienst feiern dürfen?“ Darauf müssen wir eine Antwort finden, denn in manchen Gegenden des Landes ist dies mehr als eine Empfehlung und inzwischen verpflichtend. Ich glaube, dass die Empfehlung oder Anordnung, sich in dieser Zeit nicht zu versammeln, dem Zweck dient, die Ausbreitung eines äußerst ansteckenden Virus zu verhindern; damit erfüllen wir die Schriftstelle „Liebe deinen Nächsten wie dich selbst“. Es ist eine gute Gelegenheit, der Öffentlichkeit zu zeigen: Wenn die Anordnung uns nicht dazu auffordert, gegen die Schrift zu verstoßen, entscheiden wir uns dafür, die Regierung zu achten. Bald könnte der Zeitpunkt kommen, an dem man uns auffordert, etwas zu tun, was wir nicht mit reinem Gewissen tun können; dann müssen wir standhaft bleiben und „Gott mehr gehorchen als den Menschen“.

Manche verspüren einen Anflug von Schuld wegen des Verses „unser Zusammenkommen nicht aufzugeben“. Doch scheint es dabei um eine Gewohnheit oder Lebensweise zu gehen. Ich nehme an, dass hier ein träges, faules Herz gemeint ist, das den Nutzen des Zusammenkommens nicht erkennt. Wir möchten zusammenkommen … Sobald wir wieder zusammenkommen können, werden wir diese Gelegenheit nutzen. Es ist ein großer Unterschied zwischen denen, die sich für kurze Zeit nicht versammeln können, und denen, die es nicht wollen, weil sie darin keinen Wert sehen. Derzeit scheint es das beste Zeugnis für unsere Welt und die beste Öffentlichkeitsarbeit zu sein, die Anordnung zu achten, da sie sich nicht gegen unseren Glauben und Gott richtet. Achten wir einfach darauf, dass dies nicht zu unserer neuen Normalität wird. Behalten wir einen Weg im Blick, auf dem wir wieder als örtliche Gemeinde praktisch zusammenkommen und wirken können.

Was können wir tun? Mehr denn je beten, dass Gott dies dazu gebraucht, die Verlorenen zu gewinnen und die Gemeinde zu läutern. Verbringt Zeit damit, Beziehungen zu den Menschen zu vertiefen, die euch am nächsten stehen und mit denen ihr angehalten seid, zu Hause zu bleiben. Lasst diese Pandemie uns auf das vorbereiten, was Gott für uns in der Zukunft bereithält. Lasst uns sehr darauf achten, wie wir über die Regierung und manche der während dieser Zeit erlassenen Bestimmungen sprechen. Wir sollen den König ehren, und wir müssen mehr Zeit damit verbringen, Gott für unsere Freiheiten zu danken, als uns auf das Negative zu konzentrieren: So ermahne ich nun, dass vor allem Flehen, Gebete, Fürbitten und Danksagung für alle Menschen dargebracht werden, für Könige und alle, die in hoher Stellung sind, damit wir ein ruhiges und stilles Leben in aller Gottseligkeit und Ehrbarkeit führen können. Denn dies ist gut und angenehm vor Gott, unserem Retter. –1. Timotheus 2:1-3. Für den Christen gilt: … wir wissen, dass denen, die Gott lieben, alle Dinge zum Guten mitwirken, denen, die nach seinem Vorsatz berufen sind. –Römer 8:28.

Greetings of love in the name of Jesus, our Savior, our Redeemer, and our Lord. When our last magazine issue went out, most things in the world seemed to be continuing quite normally. Suddenly, everything started changing with unnerving speed and uncertainty. The next thing we knew a previously unheard-of virus had everyone’s attention. How our lives have changed.

Knowing this first, that there shall come in the last days scoffers, walking after their own lusts, And saying, Where is the promise of his coming? for since the fathers fell asleep, all things continue as they were from the beginning of the creation –2Pe 3:3-4. I had to think of this verse as Covid-19 started upending basically all of life. Where did the church find itself during this all? Surely, we weren’t scoffing… Hopefully we weren’t walking after our own lusts… But where were we? Maybe some of us had become lulled into the belief that things would continue according to what we understood as normal, at least for our indefinite future.

But suddenly what was once normal was gone. Schools closed—forcing many families to oversee their children’s education at home. Businesses closed—forcing many folks to find a way to work from home. Libraries closed—forcing folks to read at home. Daycare centers closed—forcing many parents to find a way for at least one of them to watch their own children at home. All personal care facilities (barber shops, nail parlors, etc.) closed—forcing many families to figure out how to take care of themselves and each other at home. All centers of entertainment closed—forcing families to start entertaining themselves and each other at home.

More and more families were required to stay at home without the opportunity of interacting with others. Many were the negative predictions by professionals, authorities, and the media—Domestic Violence would rise, Child Abuse would escalate, Addictions would increase, and Mental Illness would become a major problem.

As I am writing this, our state of Ohio has started relaxing the “stay at home” order, yet no matter how much someone may wish or worry, the old normal has yet to be willed back into existence. As time has passed, new normals have begun to develop. And yes, some of the negative predictions did come to pass, yet in the middle of it all some surprises have arisen as well.

**************************************

Recently, I came across an interesting article1 published by CNN titled, WHY SOME KIDS ARE HAPPIER RIGHT NOW, AND OTHER UNEXPECTED EFFECTS OF QUARANTINE. Surprisingly, this article didn’t appear to go viral nor did it seem to generate much attention in the media. To me, this type of information should be of interest to parents and children across the whole world, yet for some reason it didn’t seem to be the type of news that the majority of the media wanted to focus on.

Information like this runs counter to the direction the world is going. It would undermine way too much of the accepted system—daycare centers for children of working parents would go out of business; mothers would need to give up their careers and instead be stay-at-home moms; extra-curricular and after school activities for all the children in any given community would no longer be needed; children being raised by the system would instead be raised by their parents; emotional and mental struggles would no longer be treated primarily with therapy and drugs, and the list could go on.

Now on to the news article. In spite of their misgivings and apprehension about all the possible negatives of the whole family being at home together most of the time, hundreds of families from around the United States … shared on social media and in discussion boards a sense of relief and joy regarding the actual outcome after some time had passed. This outcome was unexpected by most, yet according to the research of professionals, it tracks with what we [they] know about the causes of childhood anxiety and depression today. This article states that according to the research one of the most well-supported explanations for this rise of mental health disorders is that children have too much going on and not enough choice over what they do. It’s a function of a whole society that is overworked and time-poor, and our kids are paying the price for it.

This article quoted parents from across the United States, including North Carolina, Tennessee and California. It discussed an interesting phenomenon, which was referred to as a happiness spike, among children during this unexpected disruption of normal hectic schedules. Much to their surprise and appreciation, the outcome of this happiness spike was counter-intuitive to what parents had fully expected would result.

According to one parent, the whole family now eats three unrushed and healthy meals together every day; the children are sleeping more and they are having a chance to get bored and then also having time to find a solution on their own. Finally, since they are going through this time of uncertainty and heightened emotion together, it has given them something to bond over.

Peter Gray, research professor of psychology at Boston College and author of the book FREE TO LEARN, says that “Suddenly kids are being able to [be self-directed]. They have time on a nice spring day to just sit outside and enjoy the sunshine. The things that are the subject of poetry that we have been denying our children are suddenly available to them. He believes that children need to develop healthily and happily—[have] time to play and explore.

A number of things were listed which parents, psychologists, and researchers see as results of this disruption in the normal schedules for many families.

  • They are seeing more of their parents
  • They have become better behaved
  • There is an increased camaraderie among siblings.
  • They are kinder to one another
  • They are playing more alone or with siblings
  • They are less emotionally overwhelmed
  • They are sleeping better

They talked about how children could now be children since they were no longer in the rat race of life. They now had time to explore their world, in their way. They had time to use their imagination and creativity. They were no longer under the pressure of rushing from one adult-scheduled appointment to another. No longer were they under the pressure to achieve a certain level or performance based on their peers. The article says that research shows that all these small acts can give them [children] a much-needed confidence boost.

According to the news article, the sense that they [children] are in control of their own lives and can handle disruptions on their own [is] a crucial element of emotional well-being. And surprise of surprises, emotional struggles and mental disorders started to correct themselves. According to one mother, her 12-year-old daughter who had been diagnosed with ADHD and with Autism Spectrum Disorder, began to see marked improvement after about two weeks. The change was so pronounced that the negative behavior that had been part of this girl’s identity due to her diagnosed disorders, actually began to return to that of a normal 12-year-old girl.

Bottomline… hundreds of families from around the United States are reporting that their children seem happier.

******************************************

While we realize that this is according to secular wisdom, most of it is simple, common sense derived from unbiased observation of the facts. Many of these conclusions are supported by the simple teaching of God’s Word, the Holy Bible. It is interesting to me how so many in the church today want to follow in the footsteps of the world when it comes to family structure, personal development, and child rearing. Some in the church have seemed to get to a point where they feel that God’s teaching is too simple, too old-fashioned, or for some other reason they believe it just doesn’t work to accomplish a successful outcome.

My goal in highlighting this news article is to help us see that the world’s system isn’t all its cracked up to be. It doesn’t produce the kind of fruit that we all are striving for. Let’s get back to believing in the Holy Scriptures, following them in simple obedience, and believing that God’s ways will work even in our times of uncertainty.

I will close with several thoughts that I wish to leave with us all. Within the last several weeks, I heard several thoughts that were shared by two different ministers. Both were regarding this virus issue and the world-wide disruption of normal schedules. First, even though this has seemed like a major obstacle for many of us to overcome, we can be sure that this will not be the last, nor will it be the worst. We can expect to face much more difficult situations as the end of time draws ever closer. Second, is the thought that we should look at this as a wake-up call to our spiritual lives. And that there should be NO person who doesn’t allow this to bring about change in their lives. There is NO human being that is so holy that they have no need of improvement where God is concerned.

우리의 구주요 구속자요 주님이신 예수님의 이름으로 사랑의 인사를 드립니다. 지난 호 잡지가 발행되었을 때만 해도 세상은 대부분 꽤 평온하게 흘러가는 듯했습니다. 그런데 갑자기 모든 것이 불안할 만큼 빠른 속도로, 불확실하게 변하기 시작했습니다. 어느새 이전에는 들어본 적도 없던 바이러스가 모든 사람의 관심을 사로잡았습니다. 우리의 삶은 얼마나 달라졌는지요.

먼저 이것을 알라 말세에 조롱하는 자들이 와서 자기의 정욕을 따라 행하며 이르되 주께서 강림하신다는 약속이 어디 있느냐 조상들이 잠든 이래로 만물이 창조의 시작부터 그대로 있다 하니 –벧후 3:3-4. 코로나19가 사실상 삶의 모든 것을 뒤흔들기 시작했을 때 저는 이 구절을 떠올려야 했습니다. 이 모든 상황 속에서 교회는 어디에 있었을까요? 분명 우리는 조롱하고 있지는 않았겠지요… 바라건대 자기 정욕을 따라 행하고 있지도 않았기를 바랍니다… 그렇다면 우리는 어디에 있었을까요? 어쩌면 우리 중 일부는 적어도 막연한 미래까지는 우리가 정상이라고 여기는 대로 일이 계속될 것이라는 믿음에 젖어 있었을지도 모릅니다.

그러나 갑자기 한때 정상이었던 것이 사라졌습니다. 학교가 문을 닫아 많은 가정이 집에서 자녀의 교육을 지도해야 했습니다. 사업장이 문을 닫아 많은 사람이 재택근무 방법을 찾아야 했습니다. 도서관이 문을 닫아 사람들은 집에서 책을 읽어야 했습니다. 어린이집이 문을 닫아 많은 부모가 적어도 부모 중 한 명이 집에서 자녀를 돌볼 방법을 찾아야 했습니다. 모든 개인 관리 시설(이발소, 네일숍 등)이 문을 닫아 많은 가정은 집에서 자신과 서로를 돌볼 방법을 궁리해야 했습니다. 모든 오락 시설이 문을 닫아 가족들은 집에서 스스로, 또 서로를 즐겁게 해 줄 방법을 찾기 시작해야 했습니다.

점점 더 많은 가정이 다른 사람들과 교류할 기회도 없이 집에 머물러야 했습니다. 전문가와 당국, 언론은 부정적인 예측을 쏟아냈습니다. 가정 폭력이 증가하고, 아동 학대가 심해지며, 중독이 늘고, 정신 질환이 심각한 문제가 되리라는 것이었습니다.

제가 이 글을 쓰는 지금, 오하이오주는 ‘자택 대기’ 명령을 완화하기 시작했습니다. 그러나 누군가 아무리 바라거나 걱정한다고 해도, 예전의 정상적인 일상은 의지만으로 되돌아오지 않았습니다. 시간이 흐르면서 새로운 일상이 자리 잡기 시작했습니다. 물론 부정적인 예측 중 일부는 현실이 되었지만, 그 모든 상황 가운데 뜻밖의 일들도 일어났습니다.

**************************************

최근 저는 CNN에 실린 흥미로운 기사1를 접했습니다. 제목은 ‘지금 더 행복해진 아이들, 그리고 격리의 뜻밖의 영향’이었습니다. 놀랍게도 이 기사는 널리 퍼지지도, 언론의 큰 관심을 끌지도 않은 듯했습니다. 제 생각에 이런 정보는 전 세계의 부모와 아이들이 관심을 가져야 할 내용인데, 어째서인지 대다수 언론이 주목하고 싶어 하는 종류의 뉴스는 아니었던 것 같습니다.

이와 같은 정보는 세상이 나아가는 방향과 상반됩니다. 현재 당연하게 받아들여지는 체제를 너무 많이 약화시킬 것입니다. 맞벌이 부모의 자녀를 위한 어린이집은 문을 닫게 될 것이고, 어머니들은 직업을 포기하고 대신 집에 머무는 엄마가 되어야 할 것입니다. 어느 지역사회에서든 아이들을 위한 방과 전후 활동이나 과외 활동은 더 이상 필요하지 않게 될 것이며, 체제가 키우는 아이들은 부모가 직접 키우게 될 것입니다. 정서적·정신적 어려움도 더는 주로 상담과 약물로 치료되지 않을 것입니다. 그 밖에도 계속 열거할 수 있습니다.

이제 그 뉴스 기사로 넘어가겠습니다. 온 가족이 대부분의 시간을 함께 집에서 보내면서 생길 수 있는 모든 부정적인 결과를 우려하고 걱정했음에도, 미국 전역의 수백 가정이 … 실제로 시간이 조금 지난 뒤 나타난 결과에 대해 안도감과 기쁨을 소셜 미디어와 토론 게시판에서 나누었습니다. 대부분이 예상하지 못했던 결과였지만, 전문가들의 연구에 따르면 이는 오늘날 아동 불안과 우울증의 원인에 대해 우리가 [그들이] 알고 있는 것과 일치합니다. 이 기사는 연구에 따르면 정신 건강 장애가 증가한 현상에 대해 가장 충분한 근거가 뒷받침하는 설명 가운데 하나는 아이들이 너무 많은 일을 하면서도 자신이 무엇을 할지 선택할 여지가 충분하지 않다는 것입니다. 이는 과로하고 시간이 부족한 사회 전체의 문제이며, 그 대가를 우리 아이들이 치르고 있습니다.

이 기사에는 노스캐롤라이나, 테네시, 캘리포니아를 비롯한 미국 전역의 부모들이 인용되었습니다. 평소의 부산한 일정이 뜻밖에 중단된 동안 아이들에게서 나타난 흥미로운 현상을 다루었는데, 이를 행복감의 급증이라고 불렀습니다. 부모들은 놀라움과 고마움을 느꼈습니다. 이러한 행복감의 급증은 부모들이 당연히 예상했던 결과와는 정반대였기 때문입니다.

한 부모의 말에 따르면, 이제 온 가족이 매일 서두르지 않고 건강한 식사를 세 끼 함께 합니다. 아이들은 더 많이 자고, 지루해할 기회를 얻은 다음 스스로 해결책을 찾을 시간도 갖고 있습니다. 마지막으로, 불확실하고 감정이 고조된 이 시기를 함께 겪고 있으므로 서로의 유대를 다질 무언가가 생겼습니다.

보스턴 칼리지 심리학 연구 교수이자 『자유롭게 배우기』의 저자인 피터 그레이는 이렇게 말합니다. “갑자기 아이들은 [스스로 방향을 정할] 수 있게 되었습니다. 화창한 봄날 바깥에 그냥 앉아 햇살을 즐길 시간이 있습니다. 우리가 아이들에게서 빼앗아 왔던, 시의 소재가 되는 것들이 갑자기 아이들에게 주어졌습니다. 그는 아이들이 건강하고 행복하게 발달하려면—[아이들에게는] 놀고 탐험할 시간이 필요합니다.

많은 가정의 평소 일정이 흐트러진 결과로 부모와 심리학자, 연구자들이 꼽은 몇 가지 변화가 나열되었습니다.

  • 아이들은 부모와 더 많은 시간을 보냅니다.
  • 아이들의 행동이 더 좋아졌습니다.
  • 형제자매 사이의 친밀감이 높아졌습니다.
  • 아이들은 서로에게 더 친절합니다.
  • 아이들은 혼자 또는 형제자매와 더 많이 놉니다.
  • 아이들은 감정적으로 덜 압도됩니다.
  • 아이들은 잠을 더 잘 잡니다.

아이들이 더 이상 삶의 쳇바퀴 속에 있지 않으므로 이제 아이답게 지낼 수 있게 되었다는 이야기도 나왔습니다. 이제 아이들은 자기 방식으로 세상을 탐구할 시간이 생겼습니다. 상상력과 창의력을 발휘할 시간도 생겼습니다. 어른들이 정해 놓은 약속에 맞춰 이곳저곳 서둘러 다녀야 한다는 압박도 더는 받지 않습니다. 또래에 맞춰 일정 수준에 도달하거나 성과를 내야 한다는 압박도 더는 받지 않습니다. 기사에 따르면 연구 결과, 이 모든 작은 행동이 아이들에게 [아이들에게] 꼭 필요한 자신감의 향상을 가져다줄 수 있습니다.

뉴스 기사에 따르면, 자신의 삶을 스스로 통제하며 혼자서도 변화에 대처할 수 있다는 [아이들의] 감각은 정서적 안녕의 핵심 요소입니다. 놀랍게도 정서적 어려움과 정신 장애가 저절로 호전되기 시작했습니다. 한 어머니에 따르면, ADHD와 자폐 스펙트럼 장애 진단을 받은 열두 살 딸이 약 2주 뒤부터 뚜렷하게 나아지는 모습을 보였습니다. 변화가 매우 두드러져서, 진단받은 장애로 인해 그 아이의 정체성의 일부처럼 여겨졌던 부정적인 행동이 실제로 평범한 열두 살 소녀의 행동으로 돌아오기 시작했습니다.

요점은… 미국 전역의 수백 가정이 자녀들이 더 행복해 보인다고 전하고 있다는 것입니다.

******************************************

이것이 세속적인 지혜에 따른 내용임을 우리는 알고 있지만, 대부분은 편견 없이 사실을 관찰하여 얻은 단순하고 상식적인 결론입니다. 이러한 결론 중 상당수는 하나님의 말씀인 성경의 단순한 가르침으로 뒷받침됩니다. 오늘날 교회 안의 많은 이들이 가족 구조와 개인의 발달, 자녀 양육에 관해 세상의 발자취를 따르려 한다는 점은 제게 흥미롭습니다. 교회 안의 일부 사람들은 하나님의 가르침이 너무 단순하고 너무 구식이거나, 또는 다른 이유로 성공적인 결과를 이루는 데 도움이 되지 않는다고 여기는 지점에 이른 듯합니다.

제가 이 뉴스 기사를 강조하는 목적은 세상의 체제가 그리 대단한 것이 아님을 우리가 알도록 돕는 데 있습니다. 그 체제는 우리 모두가 애쓰며 추구하는 열매를 맺지 못합니다. 성경 말씀을 다시 믿고, 단순히 순종하여 따르며, 불확실한 시대에도 하나님의 길이 역사하리라고 믿읍시다.

마지막으로 우리 모두에게 남기고 싶은 몇 가지 생각으로 글을 맺겠습니다. 지난 몇 주 동안 저는 두 명의 서로 다른 목회자가 나눈 생각을 몇 가지 들었습니다. 두 사람 모두 이 바이러스 사태와 전 세계의 일상 일정이 뒤흔들린 일에 관한 이야기를 했습니다. 첫째, 이 일이 우리 중 많은 이에게 극복해야 할 큰 장애물처럼 보였지만, 이것이 마지막도 아니고 최악도 아니라는 점을 확신할 수 있습니다. 세상의 끝이 점점 가까워질수록 훨씬 더 어려운 상황들을 맞이할 것으로 예상할 수 있습니다. 둘째, 이 일을 우리의 영적 삶을 일깨우는 경종으로 보아야 한다는 생각입니다. 그리고 누구도 이 일로 자신의 삶에 변화가 생기도록 허용하지 않는 일이 있어서는 안 됩니다. 하나님 앞에서 개선할 필요가 전혀 없을 만큼 거룩한 사람은 아무도 없습니다.
