Ci fu un periodo della mia vita in cui facevo volontariato sull’ambulanza con due stazioni locali dei servizi medici di emergenza in Pennsylvania, dove vivevo. Ero un EMT qualificato e attrezzato per aiutare una persona sofferente.

Durante i turni di servizio, ero pronto a partire in qualsiasi momento. Non sapevo mai quando il cercapersone, sempre con me, avrebbe suonato l’allarme. Di notte dormivo completamente vestito con la mia uniforme da EMT. I miei stivali erano vicino alla porta. La mia auto era parcheggiata con il retro rivolto verso casa e le chiavi erano sul comodino. Ero pronto!

Alcune notti il cercapersone non suonava mai. Altre notti, il cercapersone emetteva un forte segnale acustico, interrompendo un sonno profondo. Tutto il tempo dedicato a prepararmi dava i suoi frutti e, pochi secondi dopo l’allarme, ero già alla guida per strada. Ogni secondo contava. Dovevo essere pronto in ogni momento.

Non è un segreto che gli atleti che partecipano ai Giochi olimpici dedichino spesso gran parte della loro vita a prepararsi per le gare. Non desiderano altro che raggiungere l’obiettivo di vincere quella medaglia. Ma devono prepararsi! Non si svegliano una mattina e decidono di partire quel giorno per le Olimpiadi e gareggiare per la medaglia d’oro. Se vogliono vincere, devono prepararsi. Se vogliono conquistare quella medaglia d’oro, devono allenarsi.

Verso i 14 anni, un atleta britannico avrà deciso a quale sport dedicarsi. A quel punto, comincerà a investire tutta la sua vita nell’allenamento. Per competere ai massimi livelli occorrono un impegno, risorse e investimenti straordinari. In media, un atleta d’élite si allena sei ore al giorno, sei giorni alla settimana, dodici mesi all’anno. Il suo obiettivo? Vincere!

Un atleta ha detto: «Tutto il duro lavoro ne sarà valsa la pena, però, anche solo per gareggiare davanti al pubblico di casa, e vincere una medaglia sarebbe un sogno che si avvera».

Da cristiano del Regno, leggo una citazione del genere e dico: «Che cosa frivola e vuota». Ma a te, giovane, chiedo: se loro danno tutto ciò che hanno per vincere qualcosa di così temporaneo, che cosa stai dando tu per vincere qualcosa di così eterno? Che cosa dai per una ricompensa che durerà più di ogni cosa su questa terra, una ricompensa che ha un valore che va oltre questo mondo?

Paolo usò l’esempio di un corridore per mostrarci come dovremmo correre nella nostra vita cristiana: Non sapete che nelle gare allo stadio tutti corrono, ma uno solo ottiene il premio? Correte anche voi in modo da conquistarlo –1Co 9:24. Devi correre questa gara della vita cristiana in modo da poter vincere! Ti chiedo: ti stai preparando per vincere? Stai correndo in modo da vincere?

Consideriamo brevemente due osservazioni riguardo a un atleta olimpico e poi facciamo alcune applicazioni pratiche al nostro cammino spirituale.

Osservazione n. 1: un atleta deve fare esercizio ogni giorno.

Gli atleti professionisti non si allenano perché sono costretti. Crescono desiderando più di ogni altra cosa praticare il loro sport per il resto della vita. Ma sanno che, per farlo, è essenziale rendere l’esercizio fisico parte della vita quotidiana se vogliono vincere. Non importa se corrono, sollevano pesi o fanno una passeggiata: gli atleti in allenamento prendono l’abitudine di fare esercizio ogni giorno. È una parte della loro giornata tanto quanto lavarsi i denti o pettinarsi.

Ogni atleta è temperante in ogni cosa; essi lo fanno per ottenere una corona corruttibile, noi invece una incorruttibile –1Co 9:25. Come cristiano, se il tuo obiettivo è essere fedele fino alla fine e vincere la gara della tua vita cristiana, dovrai prendere sul serio i tuoi esercizi spirituali. In effetti, gli esercizi spirituali quotidiani sono essenziali per mantenersi in forma per questa gara intensa.

Per un cristiano, l’esercizio deve essere un’attività quotidiana. Leggi la Bibbia come se la tua vita dipendesse da questo, perché è così! Prega e rimani unito a Gesù con la stessa intenzione con cui un atleta beve liquidi. (Sapevi che bere liquidi è la parte più importante dell’alimentazione di un atleta?) Prega come se la tua vita dipendesse da questo, perché è così!

Osservazione n. 2: un atleta in allenamento ottiene i risultati che merita.

È così difficile alzarsi presto la mattina quando si è raggomitolati sotto le coperte e fuori è buio e fa freddo. Ma un atleta in allenamento sa che, se non si alza per allenarsi e fare esercizio, perderà. Sa che più si allena, maggiori sono le sue possibilità di vincere. Un atleta in allenamento sa che sarà ricompensato per il tempo dedicato alla preparazione. La scelta di fare esercizio darà dei risultati.

Affinché la giustizia della legge sia adempiuta in noi, che camminiamo non secondo la carne, ma secondo lo Spirito. Infatti quelli che sono secondo la carne hanno la mente rivolta alle cose della carne; ma quelli che sono secondo lo Spirito alle cose dello Spirito. Poiché la mente carnale è morte, ma la mente spirituale è vita e pace –Rom 8: 4-6.

Come cristiano, ciò che nutri crescerà. O nutrirai la carne, oppure nutrirai lo Spirito. Se vuoi vincere la gara e raggiungere la ricompensa di essere ristabilito nella condizione in cui eri davvero destinato a vivere, dovrai avere una mente spirituale e nutrire le cose dello Spirito. Consideriamo ora un elenco parziale di cose che, a seconda di come o perché le facciamo, determineranno se stiamo nutrendo la carne o lo Spirito.

Andare a caccia e procurarsi carne da mettere nel congelatore è un’attività del tutto naturale per sopravvivere, praticata da secoli. Ma quando vai a caccia per prendere il cervo più grande e gonfiare il tuo ego e la tua autostima, stai nutrendo la carne.

Ascoltare la musica del mondo non farà nulla per nutrire e allenare l’uomo spirituale. Ma la tua carne ne sarà ben nutrita.

Seguire e/o praticare sport a livello professionistico non ti aiuterà a vincere la gara spirituale. Anzi, perderai se nutri la carne senza pensarci.

La golosità e/o il consumo di cibi e bevande non salutari non aiuteranno il tuo uomo spirituale a crescere nel Signore. Anzi, alimenteranno soltanto il tuo desiderio di averne sempre di più. Facciamo attenzione a mangiare e bere alla gloria di Dio.

Amico mio, il semplice fatto è questo: se non perseveri nel disciplinare la tua vita spirituale, tu perderai ! Dunque, che cosa stai esercitando e nutrendo: la carne o lo Spirito? Ricorda: quando l’uomo naturale cresce, non rimane più spazio perché cresca l’uomo spirituale.

Tendere in avanti e proseguire verso la meta

Paolo dice: Fratelli, io non ritengo di aver già raggiunto il traguardo; ma faccio una cosa: dimenticando le cose che stanno dietro e protendendomi verso quelle che stanno davanti, proseguo verso la meta per ottenere il premio della celeste vocazione di Dio in Cristo Gesù –Php 3:13-14.

Nella tua vita cristiana è necessario proseguire e protendersi se vuoi vincere. Nella vita cristiana non basta fare il minimo indispensabile: Dio chiama questo tiepidezza e la Bibbia dice che Egli vomiterà dalla sua bocca una persona tiepida (vedi Rev. 3:16). Dio non cerca vincitori che si impegnano solo a metà. Cerca «più che vincitori». Nel regno di Dio non c’è posto per la tiepidezza!

Per prepararci a vincere questa gara, non possiamo farne a meno della disciplina e del sacrificio di sé. Sei una persona disciplinata nella tua vita spirituale? Come si confronta questo con il tuo lavoro fisico e i tuoi hobby? Ti alzi presto per praticare uno sport che ti piace? Ti assicuri di essere puntuale al lavoro?

Hai la stessa determinazione nell’alzarti presto e nel disciplinarti nella tua vita spirituale? Cerchi la Bibbia con lo stesso entusiasmo con cui cerchi il tuo guantone da softball? Cerchi la Bibbia con lo stesso entusiasmo con cui cerchi quella lattina di bibita? Cerchi la Bibbia con lo stesso entusiasmo con cui cerchi il fucile o l’arco per andare a caccia? Cerchi la Bibbia con lo stesso entusiasmo con cui cerchi il telefono? Dedichi più tempo alla tua vita spirituale che a vestirti e pettinarti? Ti importa di più quello che pensano i tuoi amici o quello che pensa Gesù?

C’è una grande mania dei social media di mostrare a tutti quello che fai e ottenere l’approvazione degli uomini. Guardare i post sui social media ti priverà della concentrazione spirituale. Pubblicare sui social media perché tutti vedano alimenta il desiderio di ottenere l’approvazione degli uomini.

Esistono molti siti e app di social media. Tuttavia, c’è un’app che suscita desideri simili, ma in modo più sottile. È un’app che ti permette di dire agli altri «che succede». Questa app si chiama WhatsApp. È molto utile per mandare messaggi, soprattutto ai nostri conoscenti che si trovano all’estero. Ma in WhatsApp c’è anche un pulsante chiamato Stato. Ti permette di pubblicare cose perché gli altri le vedano. Ti permette di vedere che cosa stanno facendo i tuoi amici proprio in questo momento, qual è il loro stato!

Pubblicare online le proprie attività e gli eventi della propria vita, perché il mondo li veda, è diventato un impulso irresistibile e un desiderio di attenzione: un desiderio di ottenere l’approvazione degli uomini. Se alimenti questo impulso, crescerà. Poniti queste domande: «Pubblicare il mio stato su WhatsApp dà gloria a Dio? Controllare i social media per vedere che cosa fanno gli altri e come si vestono mi avvicina a Dio? Sono più ansioso di controllare lo stato dei miei amici che di aprire la Bibbia e controllare lo stato del mio cammino con Dio?». Il tempo che trascorri al telefono ti prepara meglio a vincere questa gara?

Le richieste del tuo tempo

Quanto tempo dedichi all’esercizio? Se un atleta facesse una flessione al giorno, pensi che vincerebbe? Se un atleta che desidera disperatamente vincere quella medaglia d’oro camminasse soltanto per 1/10 di miglio al giorno, pensi che vincerebbe?

Dunque, mentre ti prepari a incontrare Dio e a vincere questa gara, ti basta leggere un versetto della Bibbia al giorno per vincere? Un minuto al giorno di preghiera con il tuo Salvatore ti basta per affrontare le intense battaglie spirituali contro il nemico?

Prenditi il tempo per leggere la Bibbia: la tua vita ne dipende per sopravvivere! Prenditi il tempo per pregare: senza non puoi correre questa gara!

«Una mattina mi alzai presto e mi precipitai
subito nella giornata;
avevo così tante cose da fare che non ebbi
il tempo di pregare.
I problemi mi piombavano addosso e ogni
compito diventava più pesante;
“Perché Dio non mi aiuta?” mi chiesi.
Lui rispose: “Non me l’hai chiesto”.
Volevo vedere gioia e bellezza, ma la giornata
proseguiva grigia e cupa;
mi chiesi perché Dio non me le mostrasse. Lui
disse: “Ma non le hai cercate”.
Cercai di entrare alla presenza di Dio; usai
tutte le mie chiavi nella serratura.
Dio mi rimproverò con dolcezza e amore: “Figlio
mio, non hai bussato”.
Stamattina mi sono svegliato presto e mi sono fermato
prima di cominciare la giornata;
avevo così tante cose da fare che dovevo
prendermi il tempo di pregare». -anonimo

Le richieste del nostro tempo non potrebbero essere maggiori. Le comodità tecnologiche stanno plasmando la nostra vita. La nostra economia in piena espansione reclama il nostro tempo. Viviamo in tempi spiritualmente pericolosi! Le richieste e le distrazioni della vita hanno ridotto il tempo che dedichi agli esercizi spirituali? Ti preoccupa che il tempo dedicato alla preghiera e alla lettura della Bibbia diminuisca perché semplicemente non hai tempo?

Elimina le distrazioni

Perciò anche noi, essendo circondati da una così grande nuvola di testimoni, deponiamo ogni peso e il peccato che così facilmente ci avvolge, e corriamo con perseveranza la gara che ci è posta davanti, –Heb 12:1.

La parola greca per peso descrive qualcosa che è un ostacolo. Ci sono attività o abitudini che ti impediscono di dare tutto ciò che hai per correre questa gara? C’è qualcosa che ostacola il tuo esercizio, la tua crescita spirituale?

La parola greca tradotta avvolge significa distrarre o fare concorrenza. Ci sono peccati che ti distraggono dalla gara? Ci sono cose che fai e che entrano in competizione con i tuoi esercizi spirituali?

Forse è la frenesia a costituire il peso che ostacola la tua gara. Forse il tuo peccato è l’apatia spirituale: l’apatia è mancanza di interesse o di preoccupazione. Ti sei addormentato spiritualmente e semplicemente non te ne importa. Forse le cose che il mondo stima molto fanno concorrenza alla tua vita ed esercizio spirituali, cose come la ricchezza, lo sport e la popolarità. Il mondo stima molto l’abbigliamento? Ti è mai capitato di andare a fare shopping e comprare un capo di abbigliamento che in realtà non ti serviva, solo perché era bello, un nuovo modello?

Forse il tuo ostacolo o la tua distrazione sono semplicemente la mancanza di una visione per il regno di Dio. La Bibbia dice che dove non c’è visione, il popolo perisce. Se non hai una visione, perirai. Detto chiaramente, perderai la gara e andrai all’inferno se non hai una visione per il Regno di Dio!

Ti incoraggio ad aprire la tua vita davanti al Signore: ponigli queste domande serie.

  • «Dio, le mie priorità sono in ordine?»
  • «Dio, do valore a ciò a cui tu dai valore?»
  • «Dio, mi manca una visione?»
  • «Dio, tendo verso cose che non durano?»
  • «Dio, sono troppo occupato a correre dietro a cose che ostacolano la mia corsa?»
  • «Dio, qual è il mio peso, qual è il mio ostacolo?»

Tutto questo riguarda il prepararci a incontrare il Signore e a prepararci al nostro destino eterno. Riguarda l’essere soldati efficaci nel Suo regno. Se rifiuti di correre bene la gara qui sulla terra e di essere fedele, pensi che Dio ti voglia in cielo?

Forse hai bisogno di cercare Dio con urgenza. Forse devi apportare cambiamenti radicali alla tua vita: al tuo programma, alla tua concentrazione, alle tue attività, alle cose a cui ti dedichi.

Nessuno conosce il momento

Tutti noi abbiamo un momento stabilito per la morte nel calendario di Dio. Non hai idea di quale giorno di quale anno il tuo nome sia segnato nel calendario di Dio. Potrebbe darsi che ti resti soltanto un’altra settimana su questa terra.

C’è anche un’altra data stabilita nel calendario di Dio che solo Lui conosce. È quel grande giorno in cui Gesù ritornerà e porrà fine a ogni vita e al tempo su questa terra. Forse quel giorno arriverà mentre tu e io siamo ancora qui. Forse arriverà la prossima settimana. Quanto sei preparato in ogni momento per il tuo appuntamento con Dio?

Gesù disse: Perciò anche voi siate pronti, perché nell’ora che non pensate il Figlio dell’uomo verrà –Mat 24:44. Il tuo appuntamento con Dio avverrà quando non ci starai pensando.

Un luogo preparato

Solo le persone preparate saranno ricompensate con questo luogo eterno perfetto, di pace e riposo, che Gesù sta preparando. Il cielo è un luogo santo e preparato, riservato soltanto a persone sante e preparate. Prova a immaginare come sarebbe se tutto ciò che è malvagio e corrotto non esistesse più. Niente ruggine. Niente decadimento. Niente dolore. Niente invecchiamento. Niente tenebre. Niente peccato. Leggi Apocalisse 21 e 22 per descrizioni vivide di questo luogo preparato: il Cielo! La Bibbia dice che non ci sarà più alcuna maledizione. Riesci a immaginare un luogo senza più maledizione? Vivendo in un luogo devastato dalla maledizione, non conosciamo nulla di diverso. Tutta la creazione geme sotto la maledizione che il peccato dell’uomo nel giardino ha portato su di noi. Ma alla fine di questa vita Dio annullerà questa maledizione! Pensaci: la morte sarà sconfitta. Il caos tornerà all’ordine. Non ci saranno fame, sete, bisogno del sole, notte, dolore, pianto, sofferenza né lacrime. Il dolore e la lotta che il peccato ha portato su questa terra semplicemente NON CI SARANNO PIÙ!

Il cielo sarà colmo della pienezza della gloria di Dio. Coloro che si saranno preparati e avranno vinto questa gara saranno proprio alla presenza di Dio: saranno come Lui! Carissimi, ora siamo figli di Dio, ma non è ancora stato manifestato ciò che saremo; sappiamo che quando Egli sarà manifestato, saremo simili a Lui, perché lo vedremo com’Egli è –1Jn 3:2.

Come il sole fisico sostiene la vita sulla terra, così Gesù, il Figlio di Dio, sosterrà la vita in cielo. Sarà la fonte di tutto ciò che occorre per vivere in cielo: sarà la fonte e il sostegno della vita e della speranza per tutta l’eternità. Ma mentre i redenti godranno della pienezza di Dio in cielo, coloro che sono all’inferno sperimenteranno l’esatto contrario e, soprattutto, l’assenza di Dio.

L’inferno è l’assenza di Dio e di tutti i Suoi attributi. Nessuna luce: soltanto tenebre fitte. Nessun fondo su cui posarsi, per effetto della gravità: soltanto una caduta senza fine. Nessuna stagione: soltanto calore intenso. Nessun riposo: soltanto un continuo digrignare i denti e urlare. Niente acqua: soltanto bocche arse e secche. Niente di bello: soltanto fiamme. Niente amore: soltanto odio per il diavolo e i suoi angeli. Niente gioia: soltanto dolore. Nessuna guarigione: soltanto dolore, dolore, dolore. Nessuna speranza: soltanto un futuro eterno di tormento e rimpianto. La maledizione nella sua pienezza, senza limiti e senza possibilità di essere annullata!

Quali saranno le tue ultime parole?

Rifletti su queste ultime parole di persone che rifiutarono il sacrificio di Cristo:

Adams, un miscredente, disse: «Sono perduto, perduto, perduto. Sono dannato per sempre». La sua agonia fu così grande che, mentre moriva, si strappò i capelli.

Sul letto di morte, sir Julian Huxley, evoluzionista inglese, biologo e ateo convinto, disse: «Dunque è tutto vero, è tutto vero».

Cesare Borgia era un famoso scrittore e politico, un pianificatore meticoloso che programmava tutto nei minimi dettagli. Quando capì che stava morendo, disse: «Quando ero in vita, ho provveduto a tutto tranne che alla morte. Ora devo morire e sono del tutto impreparato e privo di ogni risorsa».

Ma le ultime parole di chi non crede sono molto diverse da quelle di chi crede in Gesù Cristo. Quando i cristiani muoiono, spesso riferiscono, sul letto di morte, di vedere angeli. Molto spesso sentono il canto più bello che abbiano mai udito. Più si avvicinano alla morte, più il suono è bello.

Charles Spurgeon disse sul letto di morte: «Li sento arrivare!» Si mise seduto dritto sul letto e chiese: «Non li sentite? Oggi è il giorno della mia incoronazione. Vedo i carri, sono pronto a salire».

Le ultime parole di Augustus Toplady, autore del canto Rock of Ages, furono: «È tutto luce, luce, luce».

Dwight L. Moody, famoso predicatore, disse sul letto di morte: «Può essere questa la morte? Ma è meglio che vivere! La terra si allontana, il cielo si apre. Oggi è il giorno della mia incoronazione».

Quali saranno le tue ultime parole su questa terra? Ti stai preparando ogni giorno per l’eternità, la tua vera casa? Corri come se la tua vita dipendesse da questo? Il tuo destino eterno sì.

And there followed him a great company of people, and of women, which also bewailed and lamented him. But Jesus turning unto them said, Daughters of Jerusalem, weep not for me, but weep for yourselves, and for your children –Luk 23:27-28.

Our Lord began his preaching ministry in a rather usual fashion: in a church, reading from a passage of scripture, …And he began to say unto them, This day is this scripture fulfilled in your ears –Luk 4:21. Many sermons from parables to prophecies flowed from the lips of the Lord’s Anointed over the next three years, but never would we guess that His final message would end in such an abnormal fashion. The bruised, beaten, and bleeding Christ, upon being thoroughly molested and mocked, began the painstaking journey up the Via Dolorosa pathway to Golgotha. Tradition would tell us that He fell beneath His cross, but scripture does not confirm this. It is here that Jesus slows His pace to offer His last public address to the women at the side of the road bewailing His plight.

Luke is the only evangelist whose insight records this, as he often takes greater notice of the ministry of women in the life of Christ. It is from him alone that we learn of …Joanna the wife of Chuza Herod’s steward, and Susanna, and many others, which ministered unto him of their substance –Luk 8:3. It is from him that we learn of Gabriel’s visit to Mary and her inner thoughts concerning the virgin birth and her visit to Elizabeth; Anna the prophetess; the widow of Nain; the Lord’s anointing by the woman who was a sinner; and Mary and Martha’s sibling rivalry at Bethany. So it is little wonder that notice is made of the fulfillment of prophecy by the female gender—…they shall look upon me whom they have pierced, and they shall mourn for him, as one mourneth for his only son, and shall be in bitterness for him, as one that is in bitterness for his firstborn. In that day shall there be a great mourning in Jerusalem … And the land shall mourn, every family apart; the family of the house of David apart, and their wives apart; … and their wives apart; … and their wives apart; … and their wives apart; … every family apart, and their wives apart –Zec 12:10-14.

These wives apart being of the gentler nature are traditionally more capable of offering sympathy and tears than their male counterparts. Thus, who in time of sorrow could refuse their gentle touch, their passionate condolences, and their empathetic pity? Our Lord! He whom we oft find bestowing great compassion on the multitudes, certainly can be touched with the feeling of our infirmities. Yet herein is found the resisting and rebuking of the offerings of lamentation from His female encouragers. Has He become insensitive in His last hour? Since He is God’s own Son, the Lamb without blemish, we must not reckon it so.

Though their tears would seem rather to be chosen than the rabble cry for crucifixion, Christ pronounced their offering defective. We must distinguish this crowd of women to be a different sort than the …many women [who] were there beholding afar off… –Mat 27:55. I would suggest that these are Jerusalem sympathizers: professional weepers who would forget tomorrow that they had wept today. These fickle ladies, adept at making loud wailing, found their way to the house of Jairus before Christ’s arrival. When He pronounced that the dead was not dead, but [that she] sleepeth –Mar 5:39, they immediately ceased their weeping ado; And they laughed him to scorn… –Mar 5:40. This, of course, is but personal surmising, but the prophetic injunction consummating this discourse concerning the impending destruction of Jerusalem, and the evil days to come, were not directed to His followers (they were instructed to flee) but to the resistant Jews.

And so, He deftly rebukes them—Weep Not!

One will not decry their natural empathy. Our emotions are as fleeting as the environment that creates them. We can feel so tender at a given moment without an ounce of the Holy Ghost. We may assume that our passionate tears are flowing from a heart of flesh, but moisture may as well be condensed upon a cold heart of stone. Jesus admonishes them soundly for their weeping. This is not just a gentle reminder, “You shouldn’t worry about me, I’ll be OK.” We see here a forceful rebuke commanding them to weep not. Their well-meant tears were falling on unfruitful soil and Christ will not have it so. Jesus does not condemn sentimental expressions, and certainly does not denounce sympathy and weeping with and for others in their time of suffering. But the tears of these women were only muddying up the path, for they were shed for the injustice, personal loss, and pain they felt. They liked this man. He went about doing good deeds. They hoped that He would free them from Roman tyranny.

“A moment to give a loose to grief,
Let grateful sorrows rise,
And wash the bloody stains away
With torrents from your eyes.
Oh, come and mourn with me awhile;
Oh, come to the Savior’s side.
Oh come, together let us mourn:
Jesus, our Lord, is crucified.
Have we no tears to shed for Him,
While soldiers scoff and Jews deride?
Ah! Look how patiently He hangs;
Jesus, our Lord, is crucified.”

While these shortsighted ancient words call us to weep over our Lord, He himself does not. So oft we find ourselves in parallel situations and refuse to see our own renegade tears. We cry from the depths of pain wrought by emotional, physical, spiritual, and mental anguish. This is but natural. A Hollywood film or a frivolous novel may move us to the same condition of heart. Emotional sympathy excites no sin, but the farewell address of our Lord bids us to look elsewhere to plant our tears and so he beckons us to “weep not for me.”

When we behold the suffering of our Lord, we must look to something else—The Cross!

In His suffering for us, we must see that He is doing exactly what He voluntarily came to do—I am the good shepherd: the good shepherd giveth his life for the sheep … Therefore doth my Father love me, because I lay down my life, that I might take it again –Joh 10: 11-17. While the band of women wailed and grieved, God looked down and smiled—Yet it pleased the LORD to bruise him; he hath put him to grief: when thou shalt make his soul an offering for sin, he shall see his seed, he shall prolong his days, and the pleasure of the LORD shall prosper in his hand. He shall see of the travail of his soul, and shall be satisfied… –Isa 53:10-11. This current scene had long ago been instated …by the determinate counsel and foreknowledge of God, ye have taken, and by wicked hands have crucified and slain: –Act 2:23. Though Peter’s quick feelings rejected the mention of it, …but for this cause came I unto this hour –Joh 12:27. Like Peter, we weep and resist Christ carrying the timber for fear that we should have to shoulder it as well. Here is the God-ordained apex of human salvation and it was being met with regret. The Son had ‘set His face as a flint’ to conquer the sin of the world. Shall we dilute it with our tears? Herein we are called to a major paradigm shift.

Weep not over the crucifixion but consider our transgressions that nailed Him there. Weep not over the dying Savior but bewail the sinner. Shed no tears upon the surgeon’s knife but grieve the spreading tumor which that knife must cut away. Bewail not the remedy for sin but mourn for the root of it. Cherish not the old rugged cross but lament the old ribald cause. Christ willingly endured the cross for the joy set before Him. Spiritual wisdom will demand that we fling our intuitions to the wind and shout for joy. The cross in not an emblem demanding our sympathy but is the divine expression of His love for us. Jesus chose the cross, came for the cross, prayed for the cross, then ultimately conquered sin by personally experiencing the cross. This is no cause for weeping. Nowhere are we instructed to feel sorry for our Lord.

Our dying Lord exhorts us, Weep not for me, but weep for...

…Yourselves

We are the cause for such a livid scene, and every honest heart will lament and feel the sting for the pain that we have caused. Eloi, Eloi, lama sabachthani (Mar 15:34), is resting upon our own heads. His God forsook Him because of our transgressions. Our pride-stained relationships, presumption, and rebellion drove Him to such a plight.

‘Twas you, my sins, my cruel sins,
His chief tormentors were.
Each of my crimes became a nail,
And unbelief the spear.
‘Twas you that pulled the vengeance down
Upon His guiltless head:
Break, break, my heart, oh burst my eyes!
And let my sorrows bleed.
Strike, mighty grace, my flinty soul,
Till melting waters flow,
And deep repentance drowns
My eyes in sorrow and in woe.” –Watts

Funerals are a traditional cause for weeping. Each of us shall slowly pass by the bier and numbly stare into the corpse of our own sinful nature staring back at us. All the vain things that have charmed us most lay mortified within the vault. Our final tear-stained farewell must be said to self-love, self-interest, self-centeredness, self-confidence, and self-pity as we stretch to entertain the final words of our Lord.

Thus, might I hide my blushing face,
While His dear cross appears.
Dissolve my heart in thankfulness,
And melt my eyes to tears. –Watts

…Your Children

Not only are we accountable for the Roman spear that pierced His side, but we must consider the Jews who spoke on our behalf that notable day—…His blood be on us, and on our children –Mat 27:25. How little we have considered the thundercloud of divine wrath that we have evoked upon our children. Many parents will pass off the neglected responsibility that they have toward the spiritual wellbeing of their offspring. None of us can change the mistakes that we have made in the training of our children, but the least we can do is spend our days weeping over the poor example we have been and difficulty we have created for their conversion. As the environment around us continues to decay and crumble, we should carefully and tearfully consider their future at every turn. Job did. How much more should we? …when the land sinneth against me by trespassing grievously, then will I stretch out mine hand upon it, and will break the staff of the bread thereof … Though Noah, Daniel, and Job, were in it, as I live, saith the Lord GOD, they shall deliver neither son nor daughter; they shall but deliver their own souls by their righteousness –Eze 14: 13-20.

…The Sin of the Nation

For, behold, the days are coming, in the which they shall say, Blessed are the barren, and the wombs that never bare, and the paps which never gave suck. Then shall they begin to say to the mountains, Fall on us; and to the hills, Cover us. For if they do these things in a green tree, what shall be done in the dry? –Luk 23: 29-31.

In the remnant portion of His message, Christ prophesies of the coming national destruction of Jerusalem. This abomination brought Jerusalem to desolation in 70 A.D. and no atrocity has surpassed it since. Our own nation stands on the brink of the judgment of God and what shall our portion be? Shall we spend our hours lobbying for better leaders, religious perseverance, and anti-abortion/anti-gay agendas? We would better spend our time alongside Daniel, Nehemiah, Ezra, and countless others confessing our sin and the sin of our people Israel, and presenting our supplication before the LORD our God. (see Daniel 9:4-20)

…Fellow Believers

Oh that my head were waters, and mine eyes a fountain of tears, that I might weep day and night for the slain of the daughter of my people –Jer 9:1. We need not look far to be disappointed by the lives of our fellow believers, for some are already turned aside after Satan –1Ti 5:15. It takes no spiritual mind to judge and label such folly. It is perfectly natural to become sarcastic, shake the head, and proclaim their error unto others. It takes love and concern to shed the penitential tear on their behalf. King Saul had turned back from following the Lord and …it grieved Samuel; and he cried unto the LORD all night –1Sa 15:11.

…Impenitent Sinners

Those of us who can find tears for the dying Saviour should indeed reserve them for the souls to whom death is but the beginning of evils. These souls carry in their bosom the instrument of their own destruction. Sin is the cross to which the soul will be fastened, and habits and depravities are the nails! The soul is bearing its sin, and loving to bear it! Look, it is going to execution, but at each step it laughs! Every step it takes is bearing it towards hell, and yet it makes mirth! Lo, the infatuated one scoffs at the voice that warns him, and every scoff he utters is increasing his guilt! Look forward to its end, its never-ending end; look forward to it steadily, with calm and tearful gaze – is it not an awful spectacle? But what if you should be beholding yourselves as in a vision, or seeing your child in the glass of prophecy? If it is your case, I beseech you repent of your sins, bewail your condition, and fly to Christ for shelter! And if it is your child, give heaven no rest; plead continually at the throne of grace till you have brought down a blessing from God upon your offspring! Never cease to pray until your sons and your daughters are safely landed on the Rock of Ages, and so secured there that they will need no other rock to hide them in the day when Christ shall come. –unknown

…Eternal Tears

Several years ago, hordes of humanity flocked the theaters and wept at Mel Gibson’s motion picture—The Passion of Christ—but few wept over their own sin. Many will say, “Lord, Lord, did I not weep at the scene? Did I not bewail your pathetic condition?” Jesus wept in Gethsemane, over Jerusalem, and at the tomb of Lazarus. But Christ’s tears were eternal and void of every wrongful motive and selfish intent. How natural to soak our couch with tears when our feelings are hurt. We fight pangs of pity at the loss of a loved one or our reputation. These are earthly tears. If God were to …put thou my tears into thy bottle… –Psa 56:8, what would He label it? For godly sorrow worketh repentance to salvation not to be repented of: but the sorrow of the world worketh death –2Co 7:10.

Eine große Volksmenge folgte ihm, auch Frauen, die um ihn klagten und trauerten. Jesus aber wandte sich zu ihnen und sprach: Töchter Jerusalems, weint nicht über mich, sondern weint über euch und eure Kinder –Luk 23:27-28.

Unser Herr begann seinen Verkündigungsdienst auf recht gewöhnliche Weise: in einer Synagoge, indem er aus einer Schriftstelle las: …Und er fing an, zu ihnen zu sagen: Heute ist diese Schrift vor euren Ohren erfüllt –Luk 4:21. In den folgenden drei Jahren gingen viele Predigten, von Gleichnissen bis zu Prophezeiungen, über die Lippen des Gesalbten des Herrn. Doch hätten wir niemals vermutet, dass seine letzte Botschaft auf so ungewöhnliche Weise enden würde. Nachdem der zerschundene, geschlagene und blutende Christus gründlich misshandelt und verspottet worden war, begann er den mühsamen Aufstieg auf dem Weg der Schmerzen nach Golgatha. Der Überlieferung zufolge fiel er unter seinem Kreuz, doch die Schrift bestätigt dies nicht. Hier verlangsamt Jesus seinen Schritt, um den Frauen am Straßenrand, die sein Schicksal beklagen, seine letzte öffentliche Ansprache zu halten.

Lukas ist der einzige Evangelist, der dies in seinem Bericht festhält, denn er schenkt dem Dienst der Frauen im Leben Christi oft größere Beachtung. Nur von ihm erfahren wir von …Johanna, der Frau des Chuza, des Verwalters des Herodes, und Susanna und vielen anderen, die ihm mit ihrer Habe dienten –Luk 8:3. Von ihm erfahren wir auch von Gabriels Besuch bei Maria und ihren inneren Gedanken über die jungfräuliche Geburt und ihren Besuch bei Elisabeth; von der Prophetin Hanna; der Witwe von Nain; davon, wie der Herr von der Frau gesalbt wurde, die eine Sünderin war; und von der Geschwisterrivalität zwischen Maria und Marta in Bethanien. So ist es nicht verwunderlich, dass die Erfüllung der Prophezeiung durch das weibliche Geschlecht Erwähnung findet: …Sie werden auf mich blicken, den sie durchbohrt haben, und sie werden um ihn trauern, wie man um einen einzigen Sohn trauert, und werden bitter um ihn klagen, wie man bitter um seinen Erstgeborenen klagt. An jenem Tag wird es in Jerusalem große Trauer geben … Und das Land wird trauern, jede Sippe für sich; die Sippe des Hauses David für sich und ihre Frauen für sich; … und ihre Frauen für sich; … und ihre Frauen für sich; … und ihre Frauen für sich; … jede Sippe für sich und ihre Frauen für sich –Sach 12:10-14.

Diese Frauen für sich sind von sanfterer Natur und traditionell eher dazu fähig, Mitgefühl und Tränen zum Ausdruck zu bringen als ihre männlichen Gegenstücke. Wer also könnte in Zeiten der Trauer ihre sanfte Berührung, ihre leidenschaftliche Anteilnahme und ihr mitfühlendes Mitleid zurückweisen? Unser Herr! Er, von dem wir oft sehen, wie er den Volksmengen großes Erbarmen erweist, kann gewiss mit dem Gefühl für unsere Schwachheiten berührt werden. Und doch finden wir hier, wie er die Klage seiner weiblichen Trösterinnen zurückweist und tadelt. Ist er in seiner letzten Stunde gefühllos geworden? Da er Gottes eigener Sohn ist, das Lamm ohne Makel, dürfen wir das nicht annehmen.

Obwohl ihre Tränen eher gut gemeint zu sein schienen als der Ruf des Pöbels nach Kreuzigung, erklärte Christus ihr Angebot für mangelhaft. Wir müssen diese Frauenschar von einer anderen Gruppe unterscheiden als den …vielen Frauen, die von ferne zusahen… –Mat 27:55. Ich würde vermuten, dass es sich um Jerusalemerinnen handelt, die mit ihm sympathisierten: berufsmäßige Klagefrauen, die morgen vergessen würden, dass sie heute geweint hatten. Diese wankelmütigen Frauen, die geübt darin waren, laut zu klagen, fanden sich im Haus des Jairus ein, noch bevor Christus dort ankam. Als er erklärte, die Tote sei nicht tot, sondern schlafe –Mar 5:39, hörten sie sofort mit ihrem Wehklagen auf; Und sie verlachten ihn… –Mar 5:40. Das ist natürlich nur meine persönliche Vermutung, doch die prophetische Ermahnung, die diese Rede über die bevorstehende Zerstörung Jerusalems und die kommenden bösen Tage abschließt, richtete sich nicht an seine Nachfolger (ihnen wurde gesagt, sie sollten fliehen), sondern an die widerspenstigen Juden.

Und so weist er sie entschieden zurecht: Weint nicht!

Niemand wird ihr natürliches Mitgefühl verurteilen. Unsere Gefühle sind so flüchtig wie die Umstände, die sie hervorrufen. Wir können in einem bestimmten Augenblick sehr gerührt sein, ohne auch nur einen Funken des Heiligen Geistes in uns zu haben. Wir mögen annehmen, dass unsere leidenschaftlichen Tränen einem fleischernen Herzen entspringen; doch ebenso gut kann sich Feuchtigkeit auf einem kalten Herzen aus Stein niederschlagen. Jesus tadelt sie nachdrücklich wegen ihres Weinens. Dies ist nicht bloß eine sanfte Erinnerung: „Ihr müsst euch nicht um mich sorgen, mir wird es gut gehen.“ Hier sehen wir einen scharfen Tadel, der ihnen gebietet, nicht zu weinen. Ihre gut gemeinten Tränen fielen auf unfruchtbaren Boden, und Christus will das nicht zulassen. Jesus verurteilt keine gefühlvollen Ausdrucksformen und verwirft gewiss weder Mitgefühl noch das Mit- und Um-Weinen mit anderen in ihrer Leidenszeit. Doch die Tränen dieser Frauen trübten nur den Weg, denn sie vergossen sie wegen der Ungerechtigkeit, des persönlichen Verlustes und des Schmerzes, den sie empfanden. Sie mochten diesen Mann. Er tat Gutes. Sie hofften, er werde sie von der römischen Tyrannei befreien.

„Gönnt der Trauer einen Augenblick freien Lauf,
lasst dankbare Wehmut aufsteigen
und wascht die blutigen Flecken fort
mit Strömen aus euren Augen.
O kommt und trauert eine Weile mit mir;
o kommt an die Seite des Heilands.
O kommt, lasst uns gemeinsam trauern:
Jesus, unser Herr, ist gekreuzigt.
Haben wir keine Tränen für ihn,
während Soldaten spotten und Juden ihn verhöhnen?
Ach, seht, wie geduldig er hängt;
Jesus, unser Herr, ist gekreuzigt.“

Während diese kurzsichtigen Worte aus alter Zeit uns aufrufen, um unseren Herrn zu weinen, tut er selbst es nicht. So oft befinden wir uns in ähnlichen Situationen und weigern uns, unsere eigenen fehlgeleiteten Tränen zu erkennen. Wir weinen aus den Tiefen des Schmerzes, den seelische, körperliche, geistliche und geistige Qualen hervorgerufen haben. Das ist nur natürlich. Ein Hollywoodfilm oder ein seichter Roman kann uns in denselben Gemütszustand versetzen. Mitfühlende Anteilnahme erregt keine Sünde, doch die Abschiedsrede unseres Herrn fordert uns auf, unsere Tränen anderswo zu säen, und so ruft er uns zu: „Weint nicht über mich.“

Wenn wir das Leiden unseres Herrn betrachten, müssen wir auf etwas anderes schauen – das Kreuz!

In seinem Leiden für uns müssen wir erkennen, dass er genau das tut, wozu er freiwillig gekommen ist: Ich bin der gute Hirte; der gute Hirte lässt sein Leben für die Schafe … Darum liebt mich mein Vater, weil ich mein Leben lasse, damit ich es wiedernehme –Joh 10:11-17. Während die Frauenschar klagte und trauerte, blickte Gott herab und lächelte: Doch es gefiel dem HERRN, ihn zu zerschlagen; er hat ihn leiden lassen. Wenn du seine Seele zum Schuldopfer machst, wird er Nachkommen sehen, seine Tage verlängern, und das Wohlgefallen des HERRN wird durch seine Hand gedeihen. Er wird von der Mühsal seiner Seele sehen und zufrieden sein… –Jes 53:10-11. Diese gegenwärtige Szene war längst zuvor festgesetzt worden: …den habt ihr, nach dem festgesetzten Ratschluss und der Vorsehung Gottes, genommen und durch die Hände von Gesetzlosen ans Kreuz geschlagen und getötet –Apg 2:23. Obwohl Petrus’ spontane Gefühle den Gedanken daran zurückwiesen, …doch darum bin ich in diese Stunde gekommen –Joh 12:27. Wie Petrus weinen wir und wehren uns dagegen, dass Christus das Holz trägt, aus Angst, wir müssten es ebenfalls auf unsere Schultern nehmen. Hier ist der von Gott bestimmte Höhepunkt der menschlichen Erlösung, und man begegnete ihm mit Bedauern. Der Sohn hatte sein Angesicht „wie einen Kieselstein“ fest gemacht, um die Sünde der Welt zu besiegen. Sollen wir das mit unseren Tränen verwässern? Hier sind wir zu einem grundlegenden Wandel unserer Sichtweise aufgerufen.

Weint nicht über die Kreuzigung, sondern denkt an unsere Übertretungen, die ihn dort angenagelt haben. Weint nicht über den sterbenden Heiland, sondern beklagt den Sünder. Vergießt keine Tränen über das Messer des Chirurgen, sondern trauert über den wachsenden Tumor, den dieses Messer entfernen muss. Beklagt nicht das Heilmittel gegen die Sünde, sondern trauert über ihre Wurzel. Hegt keine Zuneigung zum alten, rauen Kreuz, sondern beklagt die alte schändliche Ursache. Christus ertrug das Kreuz freiwillig wegen der Freude, die vor ihm lag. Geistliche Weisheit verlangt von uns, unsere Intuitionen in den Wind zu schlagen und vor Freude zu jauchzen. Das Kreuz ist kein Sinnbild, das unser Mitgefühl fordert, sondern der göttliche Ausdruck seiner Liebe zu uns. Jesus erwählte das Kreuz, kam um des Kreuzes willen, betete für das Kreuz und besiegte schließlich die Sünde, indem er das Kreuz persönlich erlebte. Das ist kein Grund zu weinen. Nirgends werden wir angewiesen, unseren Herrn zu bemitleiden.

Unser sterbender Herr ermahnt uns: Weint nicht über mich, sondern weint über …

… euch selbst

Wir sind die Ursache für solch eine erschütternde Szene, und jedes aufrichtige Herz wird den Schmerz beklagen und spüren, den wir verursacht haben. Eloi, Eloi, lama sabachthani (Mar 15:34) lastet auf unseren eigenen Häuptern. Sein Gott verließ ihn wegen unserer Übertretungen. Unsere von Stolz befleckten Beziehungen, unsere Anmaßung und Rebellion trieben ihn in diese Lage.

Ihr wart es, meine Sünden, meine grausamen Sünden,
die seine größten Peiniger waren.
Jedes meiner Verbrechen wurde zu einem Nagel,
und der Unglaube zum Speer.
Ihr habt den Zorn herabgezogen
auf sein schuldloses Haupt:
Brich, brich, mein Herz, o berstet, meine Augen!
Lasst meinen Kummer bluten.
Triff, mächtige Gnade, meine steinerne Seele,
bis schmelzende Wasser fließen,
und tiefe Reue meine Augen
in Kummer und Weh ertränkt.“ –Watts

Beerdigungen sind traditionell ein Anlass zum Weinen. Jeder von uns wird langsam am Totenbett vorbeigehen und wie betäubt in den Leichnam unserer eigenen sündigen Natur blicken, die uns anstarrt. All die eitlen Dinge, die uns am meisten bezaubert haben, liegen tot im Grab. Unser tränenreicher letzter Abschied muss der Selbstliebe, dem Eigennutz, der Selbstbezogenheit, dem Selbstvertrauen und dem Selbstmitleid gelten, während wir uns bemühen, den letzten Worten unseres Herrn Gehör zu schenken.

So könnte ich mein errötendes Gesicht verbergen,
wenn sein teures Kreuz erscheint.
Löse mein Herz in Dankbarkeit auf
und schmelze meine Augen zu Tränen. –Watts

… eure Kinder

Wir sind nicht nur für den römischen Speer verantwortlich, der seine Seite durchbohrte, sondern müssen auch an die Juden denken, die an jenem denkwürdigen Tag stellvertretend für uns sprachen: …Sein Blut komme über uns und über unsere Kinder –Mat 27:25. Wie wenig haben wir die Gewitterwolke des göttlichen Zorns bedacht, die wir über unsere Kinder heraufbeschworen haben. Viele Eltern schieben die vernachlässigte Verantwortung beiseite, die sie für das geistliche Wohlergehen ihrer Nachkommen tragen. Keiner von uns kann die Fehler rückgängig machen, die wir bei der Erziehung unserer Kinder begangen haben; doch das Mindeste, was wir tun können, ist, unsere Tage damit zu verbringen, über das schlechte Vorbild zu weinen, das wir gewesen sind, und über die Schwierigkeiten, die wir ihrer Bekehrung bereitet haben. Während die Umwelt um uns her weiter verfällt und zerbröckelt, sollten wir bei jeder Gelegenheit sorgfältig und unter Tränen über ihre Zukunft nachdenken. Hiob tat es. Wie viel mehr sollten wir es tun? …Wenn das Land sich schwer gegen mich versündigt und treulos handelt, dann werde ich meine Hand gegen es ausstrecken und ihm den Vorrat an Brot entziehen … Auch wenn Noah, Daniel und Hiob darin wären, so wahr ich lebe, spricht Gott der HERR, sie könnten weder Sohn noch Tochter retten; durch ihre Gerechtigkeit würden sie nur ihr eigenes Leben retten –Hes 14:13-20.

… die Sünde des Volkes

Siehe, es kommen Tage, an denen man sagen wird: Glücklich sind die Unfruchtbaren und die Leiber, die nicht geboren haben, und die Brüste, die nicht gestillt haben. Dann werden sie anfangen, zu den Bergen zu sagen: Fallt auf uns!, und zu den Hügeln: Bedeckt uns! Denn wenn man dies am grünen Holz tut, was wird dann am dürren geschehen? –Luk 23:29-31.

Im verbleibenden Teil seiner Botschaft prophezeit Christus die bevorstehende nationale Zerstörung Jerusalems. Diese Gräueltat führte 70 n. Chr. zur Verwüstung Jerusalems, und seither hat sie keine Gräueltat übertroffen. Unsere eigene Nation steht am Rand des göttlichen Gerichts, und was wird unser Anteil sein? Sollen wir unsere Stunden damit verbringen, für bessere Führer, religiöse Beharrlichkeit und eine Agenda gegen Abtreibung und Homosexualität zu lobbyieren? Besser würden wir unsere Zeit an der Seite Daniels, Nehemias, Esras und unzähliger anderer damit verbringen, unsere Sünde und die Sünde unseres Volkes Israel zu bekennen und unser Flehen vor den HERRN, unseren Gott, zu bringen. (siehe Daniel 9:4-20)

… die Glaubensgeschwister

O dass mein Haupt Wasser wäre und meine Augen eine Quelle von Tränen, damit ich Tag und Nacht weinen könnte über die Erschlagenen der Tochter meines Volkes –Jer 9:1. Wir müssen nicht lange suchen, um vom Leben unserer Glaubensgeschwister enttäuscht zu werden, denn einige haben sich schon abgewandt und sind dem Satan nachgefolgt –1Tim 5:15. Es braucht keinen geistlichen Sinn, um solchen Unsinn zu verurteilen und abzustempeln. Es ist völlig natürlich, sarkastisch zu werden, den Kopf zu schütteln und anderen ihre Fehler zu verkünden. Es braucht Liebe und Anteilnahme, um ihretwegen die Träne der Reue zu vergießen. König Saul hatte sich von der Nachfolge des HERRN abgewandt, und …Samuel grämte sich, und er schrie die ganze Nacht zum HERRN –1Sam 15:11.

… unbußfertige Sünder

Wer von uns Tränen für den sterbenden Heiland finden kann, sollte sie wahrlich für die Seelen aufheben, für die der Tod erst der Anfang der Übel ist. Diese Seelen tragen das Werkzeug ihrer eigenen Zerstörung in ihrem Inneren. Die Sünde ist das Kreuz, an das die Seele gefesselt werden wird, und Gewohnheiten und Verderbtheit sind die Nägel! Die Seele trägt ihre Sünde und liebt es, sie zu tragen! Sieh nur, sie wird zur Hinrichtung geführt, doch bei jedem Schritt lacht sie! Jeder Schritt bringt sie der Hölle näher, und doch macht sie sich lustig! Sieh, der Verblendete verhöhnt die Stimme, die ihn warnt, und jeder Hohn, den er ausstößt, vermehrt seine Schuld! Blick voraus auf ihr Ende, ihr niemals endendes Ende; blicke standhaft darauf, mit ruhigem und tränenvollem Blick – ist es nicht ein schrecklicher Anblick? Doch was, wenn du dich selbst wie in einer Vision sähest oder dein Kind im Spiegel der Prophezeiung? Wenn es dich betrifft, flehe ich dich an: Tu Buße über deine Sünden, beklage deinen Zustand und flieh zu Christus, um Zuflucht zu finden! Und wenn es dein Kind betrifft, lass dem Himmel keine Ruhe; flehe unablässig am Thron der Gnade, bis du einen Segen Gottes auf deine Nachkommen herabgebracht hast! Höre niemals auf zu beten, bis deine Söhne und Töchter sicher auf dem Felsen der Ewigkeit angekommen sind und dort so geborgen sind, dass sie keinen anderen Felsen brauchen, der sie an jenem Tag verbirgt, wenn Christus kommt. –unbekannt

… ewige Tränen

Vor einigen Jahren strömten Menschenmassen in die Kinos und weinten bei Mel Gibsons Film –Die Passion Christi–, doch nur wenige weinten über ihre eigene Sünde. Viele werden sagen: „Herr, Herr, habe ich nicht bei der Szene geweint? Habe ich nicht deinen erbärmlichen Zustand beklagt?“ Jesus weinte in Gethsemane, über Jerusalem und am Grab des Lazarus. Doch Christi Tränen waren ewig und frei von jedem falschen Beweggrund und jeder selbstsüchtigen Absicht. Wie natürlich ist es, unser Sofa mit Tränen zu durchnässen, wenn unsere Gefühle verletzt sind. Wir kämpfen mit Regungen des Mitleids, wenn wir einen geliebten Menschen oder unseren guten Ruf verlieren. Dies sind irdische Tränen. Wenn Gott …meine Tränen in deinen Krug täte… –Ps 56:8, was würde er darauf schreiben? Die gottgewollte Traurigkeit bewirkt eine Buße, die zur Errettung führt und die man nicht bereuen muss; die Traurigkeit der Welt aber bewirkt den Tod –2Kor 7:10.

There was a time in my life when I volunteered on the ambulance with two local EMS stations in Pennsylvania where I lived. I was a trained EMT and equipped to help a hurting person.

During my times of duty, I was prepared to run at a moment’s notice. I had no idea when my ever-present pager would sound an alarm. At night, I would sleep fully dressed in my EMT garb. My boots were parked by the door. My car was backed up to the house and the keys were lying on the nightstand. I was prepared!

Some nights my pager never sounded. Other nights, the pager would beep loudly, disturbing a deep sleep. All my preparation time paid off and within seconds of the alarm I was driving down the road. Every second counted. I had to be prepared at all times.

It is no secret that athletes who play in the Olympic games often dedicate most of their life toward preparing for the game. They want nothing more than to reach the goal of winning that medal. But they must prepare! They do not wake up one morning and decide to travel to the Olympics that day to compete for the gold medal. If they want to win, they need to prepare. If they want that gold medal award, they need to train.

By about the age of 14, a British athlete will have decided on which sport to focus. At that point, he will begin to pour his life into training. An incredible amount of commitment, resources, and investment is needed to compete on the highest stage. The average elite athlete trains six hours a day, six days a week, twelve months a year. His goal? To win!

One athlete said, “All the hard work will be worth it, though, to simply compete in front of a home crowd—and to win a medal would just be a dream come true.”

As a Kingdom Christian, I look at a quote like this and say, “how frivolous and empty.” But I ask you, young person: if they give everything that they have to win something so temporal, what are you giving to win something so eternal? What are you giving for a reward that will outlast anything on this earth—a reward that has value out of this world?

Paul used a runner as an example of how we should run in our Christian life: Know ye not that they which run in a race run all, but one receiveth the prize? So run, that ye may obtain –1Co 9:24. You are to run this race of the Christian life in such a way that you may win! I ask you, are you preparing to win? Are you running in such a way that you will win?

Let’s take a brief look at two observations from an Olympic athlete and then make practical applications to our spiritual walk.

Observation #1: Exercise must be an everyday occurrence for an athlete.

Pro athletes don’t train because they must. They grow up wanting nothing more than to play their sport for the rest of their lives. But to do so, they know that making exercise a part of everyday life is essential to winning. It doesn’t matter if they run, lift weights, or go for a walk, athletes in training will get into a habit of daily exercise. It is as much a part of their day as brushing their teeth or combing their hair.

And every man that striveth for the mastery is temperate in all things. Now they do it to obtain a corruptible crown; but we an incorruptible –1Co 9:25. As a Christian, if your goal is to be faithful to the end and win the race of your Christian life, then you will need to become serious about your spiritual exercises. In fact, daily spiritual exercises are essential to staying fit for this intense race.

Exercise must be an everyday occurrence for a Christian. Read your Bible as though your life depends on it—because it does! Pray and stay connected to Jesus with the same purpose of heart that an athlete drinks fluid. (Did you know that drinking fluids is the most important part of an athlete’s diet?) Pray as though your life depends on it—because it does!

Observation #2: An athlete in training gets the results he deserves.

It is so hard to get up early in the morning when you’re snuggled under the covers and it’s dark and cold outside. But an athlete in training knows that if he doesn’t get up to practice and exercise, he will lose. He knows that the more he exercises, the better chance he has of winning. An athlete in training knows that he will be rewarded for his time spent in preparing. There will be results from choosing to exercise.

That the righteousness of the law might be fulfilled in us, who walk not after the flesh, but after the Spirit. For they that are after the flesh do mind the things of the flesh; but they that are after the Spirit the things of the Spirit. For to be carnally minded is death; but to be spiritually minded is life and peace –Rom 8: 4-6.

As a Christian, what you feed will grow. You will either be feeding the flesh, or you will be feeding the Spirit. If you want to win the race and reach the reward of being restored to how you were really meant to live, then you will need to be spiritually minded and feed the things of the Spirit. Now let’s consider a partial list of things that depending how or why we do it, will determine whether we are feeding our flesh or the Spirit.

Hunting and getting meat for the freezer is a very natural activity for survival and has been done for centuries. But when you go hunting to get the biggest buck to boost your ego and self-esteem, that is feeding your flesh.

Listening to the world’s music will not do a thing to feed and exercise the spiritual man. But your flesh will be richly fed.

Following and/or playing in the professional sports world will not help you in winning the spiritual race. In fact, you will lose if you feed your flesh unheedingly.

Gluttony and/or consuming unhealthy food and drink will not help your spiritual man grow in the Lord. In fact, it will only feed your craving for more and more. Let’s be careful that whether we eat or drink we are doing it to God’s glory.

My dear friend, the simple fact remains: if you do not persevere in disciplining your spiritual life, you will lose! So, what are you exercising and feeding—your flesh or the Spirit? Remember, when the natural man grows, there is no more room for the spiritual man to grow.

Reaching Forth and Pressing Toward

Paul says, Brethren, I count not myself to have apprehended: but this one thing I do, forgetting those things which are behind, and reaching forth unto those things which are before, I press toward the mark for the prize of the high calling of God in Christ Jesus –Php 3:13-14.

There’s a pressing and a reaching that must happen in your Christian life if you want to win. You don’t just get by with doing the minimum in the Christian life—God calls that lukewarmness and the Bible says He will vomit a lukewarm person out of His mouth (see Rev. 3:16). God is not looking for half-hearted overcomers. He is looking for ‘more than conquerors’. There is no room for lukewarmness in the kingdom of God!

To prepare ourselves to win this race, we cannot get by without discipline and self-sacrifice. Are you a disciplined person in your spiritual life? How does it compare to your physical work and hobbies? Do you get up early for a physical sport you enjoy? Do you make sure you’re at your job on time?

Do you have the same drive to get up early and discipline yourself in your spiritual life? Do you reach for your Bible as eagerly as you reach for your softball glove? Do you reach for your Bible as eagerly as you reach for that can of pop? Do you reach for your Bible as eagerly as you reach for your gun or bow to go hunting? Do you reach for your Bible as eagerly as you reach for your phone? Do you spend more time focusing on your spiritual life than you do dressing yourself and combing your hair? Do you care more what your friends think or what Jesus thinks?

There’s a big social media craze to show everyone what you’re doing and gain approval of men. Viewing social media postings will rob you of your spiritual focus. Posting on social media sites for all to see feeds a craving for approval of men.

There are many social media sites and apps out there. However, there’s one app that creates similar cravings, but in a more subtle way. It’s an app that lets you tell others “what’s up”. This app is named WhatsApp. This app is very useful for texting, especially with our acquaintances who are overseas. But included in WhatsApp is a button called Status. It allows you to post things for others to see. It allows you to see what your friends are doing right now—what their status is!

Posting one’s activities and life’s events online for the world to see has become a gripping drive and craving for attention—a crave for the approval of men. If you feed this drive, it will grow. Ask yourself these questions, “Does posting my status on WhatsApp bring glory to God? Does checking social media sites to see what others are doing and how they are dressed draw me closer to God? Am I more eager to check the status of my friends than I am to open my Bible and check the status of my walk with God?” Is the time you spend on your phone making you better prepared to win this race?

The Demand for Your Time

How much time do you spend exercising? If an athlete would do one push-up a day, do you think he would win? If an athlete who desperately wants to win that gold medal would only walk 1/10 of a mile each day, do you think he would win?

So, as you prepare to meet God and win this race, is one Bible verse a day enough for you to win? Is one minute of prayer time each day with your Savior enough for you to fight the intense spiritual battles with the enemy?

Take time to read your Bible—your life depends on it for survival! Take time to pray—you cannot run this race without it!

“I got up early one morning, and rushed
right into the day;
I had so much to accomplish that I didn’t
have time to pray.
Problems just tumbled about me, and
heavier came each task;
“Why doesn’t God help me?” I wondered.
He answered, “You didn’t ask.”
I wanted to see joy and beauty, but the day
toiled on gray and bleak;
I wondered why God didn’t show me. He
said, “But you didn’t seek.”
I tried to come into God’s presence; I used
all my keys in the lock.
God gently and lovingly chided, “My
child, you didn’t knock.”
I woke up early this morning, and paused
before entering the day;
I had so much to accomplish that I had to
take time to pray.”
-anonymous

The demands for our time could not be greater. Technological conveniences are shaping our lives. Our booming economy is reaching for our time. We are living in spiritually dangerous times! Have the demands and distractions of life lessened your time in spiritual exercise? Does it concern you when your prayer time and Bible reading time diminishes because you simply don’t have time?

Remove Distractions

Wherefore seeing we also are compassed about with so great a cloud of witnesses, let us lay aside every weight, and the sin which doth so easily beset us, and let us run with patience the race that is set before us, –Heb 12:1.

The Greek word for weight describes it as a hindrance. Are there activities or habits that hinder you from giving all you have to run this race? Is there something that is hindering your exercise—your spiritual growth?

The Greek word for beset describes it as to distract or compete. Are there sins distracting you from the race? Are there things that you do that compete with your spiritual exercises?

Maybe busyness is the weight that’s hindering your race. Maybe spiritual apathy is your sin—apathy is a lack of interest or concern. You’ve gone to sleep spiritually, and you simply do not care. Maybe things the world highly esteems are competing with your spiritual life and exercise—things such as wealth, sports, and popularity. The world highly esteems clothing? Did you ever go shopping and buy a piece of clothing you didn’t really need, just because it was nice—a new style?

Maybe your weight or distraction is simply a lack of vision for the kingdom of God. The Bible says that where there is no vision, the people perish. If you do not have a vision, you will perish. Plainly stated, you will lose the race and go to hell if you do not have a vision for the Kingdom of God!

I encourage you to open your life before the Lord—ask Him these serious questions.

  • “God, are my priorities straight?”
  • “God, do I value what you value?”
  • “God, am I lacking vision?”
  • “God, am I reaching for things that don’t last?”
  • “God, am I too busy running after things that hinder my running?”
  • “God, what is my weight—what is my hindrance?”

This is all about preparing to meet the Lord and preparing for our eternal destiny. It’s all about being effective soldiers in His kingdom. If you refuse to run the race well here on earth and be faithful, do you think God wants you in heaven?

Maybe you need to get desperate with God. Maybe you need to make some radical changes in your life—changes to your schedule, your focus, your activities, your pursuits.

No Man Knows the Time

All of us have an appointed time of death on God’s calendar. You have no idea which day of which year your name is listed on God’s calendar. It could be that you have only one more week here on this earth.

There is also another appointed date on God’s calendar that only He knows. It is that great day when Jesus will return and end all life and time on this earth. Maybe that day will come while you and I are still here. Maybe it will come next week. How prepared are you at all times for your appointment with God?

Jesus said, Therefore be ye also ready: for in such an hour as ye think not the Son of man cometh –Mat 24:44. Your appointment with God will happen when you’re not thinking about it.

A Prepared Place

Only prepared people will be rewarded with this perfect eternal place of peace and rest that Jesus is preparing. Heaven is a holy and prepared place for only holy and prepared people. Try to imagine how it would be if everything evil and rotten would be non-existent. No rust. No decay. No pain. No aging. No darkness. No sin. Read Revelation 21 and 22 for graphic descriptions of this prepared place—Heaven! The Bible says that there will be no more curse. Can you imagine a place with no more curse? Living in a place that is ravaged by the curse, we know of nothing different. All creation travails under the curse that man’s sin in the garden brought on us. But at the end of this life, God will reverse this curse! Think of it—death will be stopped. Chaos will be brought back to order. There will be no hunger, no thirst, no need of sun, no night, no sorrow, no crying, no pain, no tears. The pain and struggle that sin brought to this earth will simply BE NO MORE!

Heaven will be filled with the fulness of God’s glory. Those who prepared and won this race will be in the very presence of God—they will be like Him! Beloved, now are we the sons of God, and it doth not yet appear what we shall be: but we know that, when he shall appear, we shall be like him; for we shall see him as he is –1Jn 3:2.

Just as the physical sun sustains life on earth, so Jesus, the Son of God will sustain life in Heaven. He will be the source of everything needed to live in heaven—He will be the source and sustainer of life and hope for all eternity. But while the redeemed are enjoying the fulness of God in heaven, those in hell will be experiencing the complete opposite, most of all will be the absence of God.

Hell is the absence of God and all His attributes. No light—only pitch-black darkness. No bottom of gravity—only falling. No seasons—only intense heat. No rest—only constant gnashing of teeth and screaming. No water—only parched dry mouths. Nothing beautiful—only flames. No love—only hatred for the devil and his angels. No joy—only sorrow. No healing—only pain, pain, pain. No hope—only an eternal future of torment and regret. The curse in its fullest—with no restraints and no reverse!

What Will Your Last Words Be?

Ponder these last words of people who rejected Christ’s sacrifice:

Adams, an infidel said, “I’m lost, lost, lost. I am damned forever.” His agony was so great that as he died, he tore the hair from his head.

On his deathbed, Sir Julian Huxley, an English evolutionist, biologist, and staunch atheist said, “So it is true after all, so it is true after all.”

Cesare Borgia was a famous writer and politician who was a meticulous planner and planned everything to the minutest detail. When he knew he was dying he said, “When I lived, I provided for everything except death. Now I must die, and I am totally unprepared and unprovided.”

But the final words of the unbeliever are vastly different from those who believe in Jesus Christ. When Christians die, they often report, on their death bed, of seeing angels. Quite often they hear the most beautiful singing they’ve ever heard. The closer to death, the more beautiful the sound.

Charles Spurgeon said on his deathbed: “I can hear them coming!” He sat straight up in bed and asked: “Don’t you hear them? This is my coronation day. I can see the chariots, I’m ready to board.”

The final words of Augustus Toplady, author of the song Rock of Ages were, “All is light, light, light.”

Dwight L. Moody, a famous preacher, while on his deathbed said, “Can this be death? Why, it is better than living! Earth is receding, heaven is opening. This is my coronation day.”

What will your last words be on this earth? Are you daily preparing for eternity—your real home? Are you running as if your life depended on it? Your eternal destiny does.

我人生中曾有一段时间，在宾夕法尼亚州我居住地附近的两个地方急救医疗服务站担任救护车志愿人员。我受过急救医疗技术员训练，也做好了帮助伤者的准备。

值勤时，我随时准备在接到通知后立即出发。我不知道那只始终带在身边的寻呼机会在什么时候响起警报。夜里，我会穿着整套急救人员制服睡觉。靴子放在门边。我的车倒着停在屋旁，钥匙则放在床头柜上。我已经准备好了！

有些夜晚，寻呼机始终没有响。另一些夜晚，寻呼机突然大声鸣响，打破了我的酣睡。我所做的一切准备都派上了用场，警报响起后几秒钟内，我就开车上路了。每一秒都很重要。我必须时时刻刻做好准备。

众所周知，参加奥运会的运动员往往把一生中的大部分时间都用来为比赛做准备。他们最渴望的就是实现赢得奖牌的目标。但他们必须做好准备！他们不会某天早晨醒来，才决定当天前往奥运会，参加金牌争夺赛。如果他们想赢，就得做好准备。如果他们想赢得金牌，就得训练。

英国运动员大约到了14岁，就会决定专注于哪一项运动。从那时起，他们便开始全身心投入训练。要在最高水平的赛场上竞技，需要非凡的投入、资源和付出。顶尖运动员平均每周训练六天，每天六小时，一年十二个月。他的目标是什么？赢！

一位运动员说：“不过，所有的艰苦训练都是值得的，只要能在主场观众面前参赛就好；而要是能赢得一枚奖牌，那简直就是梦想成真。”

作为一名国度基督徒，看到这样的说法，我会说：“多么轻浮而空洞。”但我要问你，年轻人：如果他们倾尽所有，只为赢得如此短暂的东西，那么你为了赢得永恒的东西，又付出了什么？为了得到一份超越世上一切的奖赏——一份价值非凡的奖赏——你付出了什么？

保罗以赛跑的人为例，说明我们在基督徒生命中当如何奔跑：你们岂不知，在场上赛跑的都跑，但得奖赏的只有一人吗？你们也当这样跑，好叫你们得着奖赏——林前 9:24。你们应当以能够获胜的方式，奔跑基督徒生命的赛程！我要问你：你是否正在为获胜做准备？你是否正以必能获胜的方式奔跑？

让我们简要看看奥运选手的两点观察，然后把它们实际应用于我们的属灵生活。

观察一：运动员必须每天锻炼。

职业运动员训练，并不是因为他们不得不练。他们从小就一心想要终身从事自己喜爱的运动。但他们知道，要做到这一点，每天锻炼是获胜的关键。无论是跑步、举重，还是散步，正在训练的运动员都会养成每天锻炼的习惯。这就像刷牙或梳头一样，是他们每天生活的一部分。

凡较力争胜的，诸事都有节制。他们不过是要得能坏的冠冕；我们却是要得不能坏的冠冕——林前 9:25。基督徒若以至终忠心、赢得基督徒生命的赛跑为目标，就必须认真操练属灵生命。事实上，每日操练属灵生命，是为了在这场激烈的赛跑中保持良好状态所不可或缺的。

基督徒必须每天操练。要读圣经，仿佛你的生命全赖于此——因为确实如此！祷告，并全心持守与耶稣的连结，就像运动员为了同样的目的而喝水一样。（你知道吗？补充水分是运动员饮食中最重要的一环。）要祷告，仿佛你的生命全赖于此——因为确实如此！

观察二：正在训练的运动员会得到应得的结果。

清晨醒来时，若你裹在被窝里，外面又黑又冷，要起床实在很难。但正在训练的运动员知道，如果不起床练习和锻炼，他就会输。他知道锻炼越多，获胜的机会就越大。正在训练的运动员知道，自己为准备所花的时间必有回报。选择锻炼，就会带来成果。

使律法的义成就在我们这不随从肉体、只随从圣灵的人身上。因为< u>随从肉体的人，体贴肉体的事；随从圣灵的人体贴圣灵的事。体贴肉体的就是死；体贴圣灵的乃是生命、平安——罗 8:4-6。

基督徒啊，你喂养什么，什么就会成长。你要么喂养肉体，要么喂养圣灵。如果你想赢得这场赛跑，并得到恢复到原本受造时应有生活状态的奖赏，就必须专注于属灵的事，喂养圣灵的事。现在，让我们来看看一份简略清单：我们做某些事的方式或动机，将决定我们是在喂养肉体还是圣灵。

打猎、把肉储存在冰柜里，是一种很自然的生存活动，几个世纪以来人们一直如此。但如果你打猎是为了猎到最大的一头雄鹿，好抬高自己的自尊和自我评价，那就是在喂养肉体。

听世俗音乐，丝毫不能喂养和操练属灵的人；但你的肉体却会大得滋养。

追随职业体育界，或参与其中，对赢得属灵的赛跑毫无帮助。事实上，如果你毫无节制地喂养肉体，就会输掉比赛。

贪食，或食用不健康的食物和饮料，都不能帮助你的属灵生命在主里成长。事实上，这只会喂大你对更多东西的渴求。无论吃喝什么，都要谨慎，叫所做的都能荣耀神。

亲爱的朋友，事实很简单：如果你不坚持操练自己的属灵生命，你 就会 输！那么，你正在操练和喂养的是什么——肉体还是圣灵？记住，天然生命一旦增长，属灵生命就再没有成长的空间。

竭力向前，奋力迈进

保罗说：弟兄们，我不是以为自己已经得着了；我只有一件事，就是忘记背后，努力面前的，向着标竿直跑，要得神在基督耶稣里从上面召我来得的奖赏——腓 3:13-14。

你若想获胜，基督徒生命中就必须有奋力和竭力。在基督徒生命中，仅仅做到最低限度是不够的——神称这为不冷不热，圣经说祂要把不冷不热的人从口中吐出去（见启 3:16）。神要找的不是半心半意的得胜者；祂要找的是“得胜有余的人”。神的国里容不下不冷不热！

为了预备自己赢得这场赛跑，我们不能没有操练和自我牺牲。你在属灵生活中是个有操练的人吗？这与身体活动和嗜好相比如何？你会为了自己喜欢的体育运动而早起吗？你会确保自己准时上班吗？

你是否同样积极地早起，在属灵生活上操练自己？你伸手拿圣经，是否和拿垒球手套一样急切？你伸手拿圣经，是否和拿汽水罐一样急切？你伸手拿圣经，是否和拿枪或弓去打猎一样急切？你伸手拿圣经，是否和拿手机一样急切？你花在关注属灵生活上的时间，是否比穿衣梳头的时间更多？你更在意朋友怎么想，还是耶稣怎么想？

社交媒体上有一股热潮，人们把自己做的事展示给所有人看，以赢得人的认可。浏览社交媒体上的帖子，会夺走你对属灵事物的专注。在社交媒体网站上发帖给所有人看，会助长渴望得到人的认可之心。

如今有许多社交媒体网站和应用程序。不过，有一个应用程序会以更隐晦的方式引发类似的渴求。它可以让你告诉别人“近况如何”。这个应用程序叫作WhatsApp。它在发短信方面很实用，尤其方便我们联系身在海外的熟人。但WhatsApp里还有一个名为“状态”的按钮，可以发布内容供别人观看，也可以看到朋友此刻在做什么——他们的状态如何！

把自己的活动和生活点滴发布到网上，供全世界观看，已经成了一种强烈的冲动，一种渴望关注的心——一种渴求他人认可的心。如果你纵容这种冲动，它就会愈发强烈。问问自己：“在WhatsApp上发布我的状态，能荣耀神吗？查看社交媒体网站，看看别人在做什么、穿什么，会使我更亲近神吗？我是否更急切地查看朋友的状态，而不是打开圣经，察看自己与神同行的状况？”你花在手机上的时间，是否让你更有准备赢得这场赛跑？

时间的要求

你花多少时间锻炼？如果运动员每天只做一个俯卧撑，你觉得他能赢吗？如果一位迫切想赢得金牌的运动员每天只走1/10英里，你觉得他能赢吗？

那么，当你准备迎见神、赢得这场赛跑时，每天读一节圣经，足以让你获胜吗？每天只用一分钟与你的救主祷告，足以让你抵挡与仇敌之间激烈的属灵争战吗？

要花时间读圣经——你的生命能否存活，全赖于此！要花时间祷告——没有祷告，你就无法跑完这场赛程！

“一天清晨，我早早起床，匆忙
投入新的一天；
要做的事多得不胜枚举，我竟然
没有时间祷告。
问题接踵而来，每一项任务
都更加沉重；
‘神为什么不帮助我？’我纳闷。
祂回答：‘你没有求。’
我想看见喜乐和美好，可这一天
在灰暗凄凉中劳碌过去；
我不明白神为何不让我看见。祂
说：‘可是你没有寻求。’
我试着来到神面前；我把所有钥匙
都插进锁孔。
神温柔慈爱地责备我：‘孩子，
你没有敲门。’
今天清晨我早早醒来，进入新的一天
之前先停了下来；
要做的事多得不胜枚举，所以我必须
抽出时间祷告。’”
-佚名

对我们时间的要求从未如此之多。科技带来的便利正在塑造我们的生活。蓬勃发展的经济不断争夺我们的时间。我们正生活在属灵上危险的时代！生活中的要求和干扰，是否减少了你操练属灵生命的时间？当你因为觉得实在没有时间，祷告和读圣经的时间减少时，你会不会担忧？

排除干扰

我们既有这许多的见证人，如同云彩围着我们，就当放下各样的重担，脱去容易缠累我们的罪，存心忍耐，奔那摆在我们前头的赛程——来 12:1。

希腊文中的重担一词指的是一种阻碍。有没有什么活动或习惯妨碍你全力奔跑这场赛程？有没有什么事妨碍你的操练——你的属灵成长？

希腊文中的缠累一词含有分散注意力或争夺之意。有没有罪使你分心，偏离赛程？你做的事中，有没有什么与属灵操练争夺你的时间和精力？

也许忙碌就是妨碍你奔跑的重担。也许你的罪是属灵冷漠——冷漠就是缺乏兴趣或关心。你的属灵生命已经沉睡，而你根本毫不在意。也许世人极为看重的事物，正在与你的属灵生命和操练争夺地位——例如财富、体育运动和受欢迎程度。世人极为看重衣着。你有没有逛街买过一件其实并不需要的衣服，只因为它好看、款式新颖？

也许你的重担或干扰，只是因为你对神的国没有异象。圣经说，没有异象，民就放肆。你若没有异象，就必灭亡。说得明白些：你若没有神国的异象，就会输掉赛跑，下地狱！

我鼓励你把生命敞开在主面前——向祂提出这些严肃的问题。

  • “神啊，我的优先次序摆正了吗？”
  • “神啊，我看重的，是否正是你看重的？”
  • “神啊，我是否缺乏异象？”
  • “神啊，我是否在追求不会长存的事物？”
  • “神啊，我是否忙着追逐那些妨碍我奔跑的事物？”
  • “神啊，我的重担是什么——我的阻碍是什么？”

这一切都是为了预备迎见主，预备面对我们永恒的归宿。这一切都是为了在祂的国里成为有用的精兵。如果你拒绝在世上好好奔跑这场赛程、忠心到底，你觉得神会愿意让你进天堂吗？

也许你需要迫切地寻求神。也许你需要在生活中作出一些彻底的改变——改变你的时间安排、关注重点、活动和追求。

无人知道那日子

在神的日历上，我们每个人都有一个被定下的死亡时刻。你不知道神的日历上把你的名字列在哪一年哪一天。也许你在这世上只剩一个星期。

神的日历上还有另一个只有祂知道的指定日期。那就是耶稣再来、终结地上一切生命和时间的伟大日子。也许那日来到时，你我还在世上；也许就在下星期。面对你与神的约会，你是否随时做好了准备？

耶稣说：所以，你们也要预备；因为你们想不到的时候，人子就来了——太 24:44。你与神的约会，会在你意想不到的时候来到。

预备好的地方

只有预备好的人，才能得到耶稣正在预备的这个完美、永恒、充满平安与安息的地方作为奖赏。天堂是圣洁、预备好的地方，只为圣洁、预备好的人存留。试着想象，如果一切邪恶、腐败的事物都不复存在，会是怎样的情景。没有锈蚀。没有腐朽。没有疼痛。没有衰老。没有黑暗。没有罪。请读启示录21章和22章，看看对这个预备好的地方——天堂——生动的描述！圣经说，再没有咒诅。你能想象一个不再有咒诅的地方吗？我们生活在受咒诅蹂躏的地方，因而想象不出别的样子。整个受造界都在叹息，因为人类在伊甸园中的罪把咒诅带给了我们。但在今生结束时，神要扭转这咒诅！想想看——死亡将被止住，混乱将恢复为秩序。没有饥饿，没有口渴，不需要太阳，没有黑夜，没有忧伤，没有哭泣，没有疼痛，没有眼泪。罪带到这世上的痛苦和挣扎将彻底不复存在！

天堂将充满神荣耀的丰盛。那些预备好并赢得这场赛跑的人，将身处神的面前——他们要像祂！亲爱的弟兄啊，我们现在是神的儿女，将来如何，还未显明；但我们知道，主若显现，我们必要像他，因为必得见他的真体——约壹 3:2。

正如有形的太阳维系地上的生命，神的儿子耶稣也将维系天堂的生命。祂将成为在天堂生活所需的一切的源头——祂将成为生命和盼望的源头与维系者，直到永远。但当蒙救赎的人在天堂享受神的丰盛时，在地狱的人所经历的则截然相反，其中最甚的，就是神的缺席。

地狱就是没有神，也没有祂的一切属性。没有光——只有漆黑一片。没有重力的尽头——只有坠落。没有季节变化——只有酷热。没有安息——只有不停地咬牙切齿、尖声哀嚎。没有水——只有干裂焦渴的嘴唇。没有美好之物——只有火焰。没有爱——只有对魔鬼和他的使者的憎恨。没有喜乐——只有忧伤。没有医治——只有痛苦、痛苦、痛苦。没有盼望——只有永远受折磨、懊悔的未来。咒诅达到极致——毫无遮拦，也无法逆转！

你在世上的遗言会是什么？

请思量这些拒绝基督牺牲之人的临终遗言：

无信仰者亚当斯说：“我迷失了，迷失了，迷失了。我永远要受诅咒。”他极其痛苦，临终时把自己头上的头发都扯了下来。

英国进化论者、生物学家、坚定的无神论者朱利安·赫胥黎爵士临终时说：“原来这一切终究是真的，原来这一切终究是真的。”

切萨雷·博吉亚是一位著名作家和政治家，做事一丝不苟，凡事都计划到最细微之处。知道自己将死时，他说：“我活着时，为一切都做了准备，唯独没有为死亡做准备。如今我必须死去，却完全没有准备，也没有安排。”

然而，不信的人临终遗言，与信靠耶稣基督的人大不相同。基督徒去世时，常常会在临终床上说自己看见了天使。他们也常常听见自己一生听过最优美的歌声。越接近死亡，声音就越动听。

查尔斯·司布真临终时说：“我听见他们来了！”他在床上直起身子问：“你们没听见吗？今天是我的加冕日。我看见战车了，我准备上车了。”

《万古磐石》的作者奥古斯都·托普雷迪最后说：“一切都是光，光，光。”

著名布道家德怀特·L·穆迪临终时说：“这会是死亡吗？怎么，死亡比活着还好！尘世渐渐远去，天堂正在敞开。这是我的加冕日。”

你在这世上的遗言会是什么？你是否每天都在为永恒——你真正的家乡——做准备？你是否仿佛生命全赖于此般奔跑？你的永恒归宿确实全赖于此。
